_securityNotes: Project Aegis: This spec contains P0 security work that fixes a confirmed remote-code-execution vector in the MCP HTTP transport. Drive-by browser fetches to /mcp currently get LOCAL_ADMIN role with access to ~414 auto-generated tools including PTY spawn, env-var injection, vault writes, and arbitrary skill install. CLI-045 through CLI-052 close this hole via Bearer token + opt-IN annotation gate + curated allow-list. Hard cutover: no backward-compat for unauthenticated MCP. CLI-034+ (workspace migration, supervisor, TUI) MUST NOT ship before CLI-045–050 land.
_openCoreNotes: Open-Core boundary: packages/rorca-cli/ is MIT/Apache (open source, viral adoption). backend/ and src/ (web UI) are BSL-1.1 (proprietary, monetization). The x-rorca-tier annotation is THE legal and commercial boundary — public-tier routes are the open-source CLI's stable API contract; paid-tier routes are paywalled at the server. The four tiers (public/auth/paid/admin) replace x-mcp-tier from the original Aegis design. CLI-053..056 enforce this at code, runtime, and license-header levels.

_tierModel.public: Open-source CLI + MCP + free web UI. Spec CRUD, story execution, local memory, recall, search. Contract is stable — breaking changes here break external CLI consumers.
_tierModel.auth: Logged-in users. Personal profiles, owned workspace settings, user preferences. Not for unauthenticated MCP clients.
_tierModel.paid: License/subscription required. Team RBAC, federated memory, GRC audit traces, multi-entity accounting, FinOps dashboards, marketplace publish. Returns 402 PLAN_REQUIRED on free plan.
_tierModel.admin: Single-user local admin. Backups, license generation, db migrations, embed-all. Never MCP-exposed. Never accessible from open-source CLI.

userStories.title: Create pi-detector.ts — binary detection, version parsing, model listing
userStories.description:
Create `backend/src/lib/pi-detector.ts` following the exact pattern of `codex-detector.ts`. The npm package is `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` — this is the correct package name used in all install instructions. The file must export: `PiStatus` interface (`{ piInstalled: boolean; piVersion: string | null; piBinPath: string | null }`), `detectPi()` that resolves binary via `PI_BIN` env var → `which pi` fallback → runs `"${binPath}" --version` with 5s timeout → parses semver from output, `requirePi()` that calls `detectPi()`, logs fatal + exits 1 if not installed, logs the correct install command (`npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`) and info with detected version. Additionally export `PiModel` interface (`{ provider: string; model: string; contextTokens: number; maxOutTokens: number; thinking: boolean; images: boolean }`) and `listPiModels(binPath: string): PiModel[]` that runs `"${binPath}" --list-models` (no `--mode json` flag — it is ignored by pi for this command) with 10s timeout and parses the ASCII table output. The ASCII table parsing uses `split('\n')`, skips header/separator lines (lines starting with `─` or `│ Provider` or empty), splits each data row on 2+ consecutive spaces (regex `/ {2,}/`), and maps to `PiModel`. Never throws — returns empty array on any error. Also export `parsePiModelTable(stdout: string): PiModel[]` as the pure parsing function (for testability). Export a `PI_INSTALL_METHODS` constant: `{ npm: 'npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent', pnpm: 'pnpm add -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent', bun: 'bun add -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent', curl: 'curl -fsSL https://pi.mariozechner.com/install.sh | sh' }` — used wherever install instructions are displayed.

## Context
- **Mirror codex-detector.ts exactly**: Read `backend/src/lib/codex-detector.ts` first and follow its structure (env var → `which` fallback → `execSync` with timeout → try/catch returns null status). Match its logging style and error swallowing — `detectPi()` must never throw.
- **Use `execSync` with `{ timeout, encoding: 'utf8' }`**: 5s for `--version`, 10s for `--list-models`. Wrap each in try/catch returning safe defaults (empty status object or `[]`). Do not use async `exec` — detectors are synchronous by convention here.
- **Semver parsing**: Use a regex like `/(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)/` against `--version` stdout; first match wins. Do not assume the binary outputs only the version string.
- **ASCII table parsing rules**: Skip lines starting with `─`, `│ Provider`, or empty/whitespace-only. Strip leading/trailing `│` before splitting on `/ {2,}/`. Coerce `contextTokens`/`maxOutTokens` via `Number()`, default to 0 on NaN. Coerce `thinking`/`images` from `'✓'`/`'✗'` or `'true'`/`'false'` strings.
- **Export `parsePiModelTable` separately**: Pure function taking raw stdout — required for unit tests without spawning the binary.
- **PI_INSTALL_METHODS must match spec exactly**: `npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` (acceptance criterion checks this string literally). Do not abbreviate or rename the package.
- **`requirePi()` exits with code 1**: Use `process.exit(1)` after `console.error` (FATAL prefix). When found, log info with both version and binPath so operators can verify which binary resolved.
- **Strict TypeScript**: No implicit `any`, no `@ts-ignore`. Type `execSync` results as `string` via the `encoding` option. Functions under 40 lines — extract `resolveBinPath()` and `runVersion()` helpers if needed.

userStories.title: Add spawnPiRpc() — warm RPC server pattern for pi execution in execution-engine.ts
userStories.description:
Add the pi warm RPC server implementation to `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts`. Architecture decision: **one pi --mode rpc process is shared across ALL stories in a spec run** (not one subprocess per story). This eliminates ~2s cold-start overhead per story. The RPC server is started before the first pi story and killed after the last.

**Step 1 — Add constants** (near CODEX_BIN):
```typescript
const PI_BIN = process.env.PI_BIN || (() => {
  try { return execSync('which pi', { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim(); } catch { return 'pi'; }
})();
```

**Step 2 — Add PiRpcServer state** (module-level, near Playwright MCP state):
```typescript
interface PiRpcServer {
  process: ChildProcess;
  requestId: number;
  pending: Map<string, { resolve: (r: unknown) => void; reject: (e: Error) => void }>;
  eventListeners: Array<(event: unknown) => void>;
  stderr: string;
  ready: boolean;
}
let _piRpcServer: PiRpcServer | null = null;
```

**Step 3 — Add JSONL helpers** (copy verbatim from pi's open-source `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/jsonl.ts`):
- `serializeJsonLine(value: unknown): string` — `JSON.stringify(value) + '\n'`
- `attachJsonlLineReader(stream: Readable, onLine: (line: string) => void): () => void` — uses `StringDecoder`, splits on `\n` only (NOT readline which splits on Unicode separators), returns cleanup fn

**Step 4 — Add `startPiRpcServer(cwd: string, model: string | null): Promise<PiRpcServer>`**:
1. If `_piRpcServer?.ready` return existing server (idempotent)
2. Build args: `['--mode', 'rpc', ...model ? ['--model', model] : []]`
3. `spawn(PI_BIN, args, { cwd, env: buildCleanEnv(), stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'] })`
4. Collect stderr into `server.stderr` buffer
5. Attach JSONL reader to stdout via `attachJsonlLineReader`. On each parsed line: if `data.type === 'response' && data.id` → resolve pending request; else → fan out to all `eventListeners`
6. Wait 200ms for process to initialize, verify `process.exitCode === null`
7. Set `server.ready = true`, assign `_piRpcServer = server`
8. Register cleanup: `process.on('exit', stopPiRpcServer)`

**Step 5 — Add `stopPiRpcServer(): Promise<void>`**:
1. If `!_piRpcServer` return
2. Send SIGTERM, wait up to 3s for exit, then SIGKILL
3. Set `_piRpcServer = null`

**Step 6 — Add `sendPiRpcCommand(server: PiRpcServer, command: object): Promise<unknown>`**:
1. Generate `id = 'req_' + ++server.requestId`
2. Write `serializeJsonLine({ ...command, id })` to `server.process.stdin`
3. Return Promise that resolves when response with matching id arrives (30s timeout)
4. On timeout: reject with Error including stderr tail

**Step 7 — Add `spawnPiRpc(prompt, cwd, timeoutMs, logFile, model, onTokenUpdate): Promise<AgentResult>`**:
1. `const server = await startPiRpcServer(cwd, model)` — gets or creates warm server
2. `await sendPiRpcCommand(server, { type: 'new_session' })` — fresh session per story (clean slate)
3. Attach transient event listener to server.eventListeners for this story's streaming events
4. Set up story timeout: `setTimeout(() => sendPiRpcCommand(server, { type: 'abort' }), timeoutMs)` — abort (not kill) preserves the server
5. Start tracking: `let storyTimedOut = false`, logStream = `fs.createWriteStream(logFile, { flags: 'a' })`
6. `await sendPiRpcCommand(server, { type: 'prompt', message: prompt })` — returns immediately; events stream async
7. Wait for `agent_end` event via Promise (the pi RPC server emits this when the turn completes)
8. **Event handling** inside the transient listener:
   - `message_update` with `assistantMessageEvent.type === 'text_delta'`: extract delta, write to `process.stdout` + logStream
   - `tool_execution_start`: log `[Tool] <toolName>: <args summary>` to stdout + logStream
   - `tool_execution_end`: log `[Tool] <toolName> done (exitCode)` to stdout + logStream
   - `turn_end`: extract `message.usage` → call `onTokenUpdate({ inputTokens: usage.input, outputTokens: usage.output, ... })`; resolve the wait
   - `agent_end`: also resolves the wait
9. Remove transient listener after resolution
10. Clear timeout. Return `{ exitCode: storyTimedOut ? 124 : 0, stderrTail: server.stderr.slice(-4096), elapsedMs }`

**Important**: The JSONL helpers can be copied verbatim from pi's open source code at `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/jsonl.ts` (MIT licensed). Do NOT use Node's `readline` module — it splits on Unicode line separators inside JSON strings, which breaks JSONL framing.

userStories.description: Create a `rorca doctor` CLI command (in `bin/rorca.ts` which will be created by CLI-025) and a standalone `GET /api/doctor` endpoint that performs a comprehensive system health check and prints actionable fixes. The doctor checks in order: (1) **Docker running** — shell out to `docker info 2>/dev/null` with 3s timeout. If not running: print `✗ Docker not running — start Docker Desktop (or OrbStack on macOS)`. If Docker missing: print `✗ Docker not found — install from https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/`. This check runs BEFORE the backend check because the backend depends on the DB which depends on Docker. (2) **Database container running** — run `docker ps --filter name=rorca-db --format '{{.Status}}'`. If not up: print `✗ Database container not running — run: rorca db start`. (3) **Backend reachable** — `GET http://localhost:3030/api/health` within 2s. If unreachable: print `✗ Backend not running — start with: rorca start` and exit further HTTP checks (all other checks need the backend). (4) **Database connected** — health response includes `{ db: true }`. If false: print `✗ Database not connected — check DATABASE_URL`. (5) **Worker running** — health response includes `{ workerLive: true }`. If false: print `✗ Worker not running — start with: cd backend && npm run worker`. (8) **At least one workspace** — `GET /api/workspaces`. If empty: print `⚠ No workspaces registered — run: rorca init`. (9) **Active agent configured** — health response `agentType`. Print current agent. Each check prints either `✓ OK`, `⚠ Warning`, or `✗ Error`. At the end, print overall status: `All checks passed` (green) or `N issue(s) found` (red). userStories.title: Session persistence: Ctrl+C safety and detached-run semantics
userStories.description: Define and implement the session persistence contract for the Forge TUI and rorca run CLI. The rule: **killing the TUI (Ctrl+C) must never kill the pi subprocess**. The pi subprocess is owned by the Rorca backend worker process, not by the TUI. The TUI is a view — it can die and the run continues. Implementation: (1) The `rorca run` CLI command and the TUI `run` command both connect to the run via SSE (GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id/output). When the TUI or CLI process receives SIGINT (Ctrl+C), it must: ask 'Cancel run? [y/N]' — if N or no input within 3s, it disconnects the SSE stream (closes the HTTP connection) and exits with code 0. The pi subprocess continues in the background, run continues. If y, it calls the cancel endpoint and waits for confirmation. (2) Add a `rorca attach <runId>` command to bin/rorca.ts. This command calls `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id` to verify the run is active, then opens SSE streams to both /api/pipeline/stream and /api/pipeline/runs/:id/output and renders the same color-coded output as `rorca run`. Useful after detaching or reconnecting after network drop. (3) The Forge TUI shows a 'Runs in background' indicator in the header when a run is active but the TUI lost its SSE connection — polls GET /api/pipeline/runs every 10s to detect active runs on startup.

userStories.title: 'board' command: inline kanban summary in the main viewport
userStories.description:
Implement the `board` command. When user types `> board`, render compact text-mode kanban in main viewport. Layout: three ASCII columns separated by `│` — PENDING | APPROVED | RUNNING/DONE. Each spec as a card: `[slug-truncated-to-28-chars]` line and `  ↳ N stories  •  pass_rate%  •  <time-ago>` line. Active runs show pulsing `●`/`○` (alternate every 500ms). Max 8 cards per column, `+N more` if overflow. `[r] run  [a] approve  [Esc] back` hint. Arrow keys navigate. `r` on approved spec triggers run. `a` on pending spec approves and refreshes. Board refreshes every 5s.

## Context
- **Reuse kanban data source**: Hit `GET /api/specs/kanban` (already returns `draft/inProgress/done` with `activeRunStatus` + `queuePosition` + story counts) — do not re-implement aggregation client-side; it was optimized 5-11x in 2026-03-16 with batch pre-fetches.
- **Slug, not title**: Card identifier must be `spec.id` (filename slug), never `spec.specName`. All downstream `r`/`a` keybindings must pass slug to run/approve endpoints (`POST /api/specs/:id/approve`, `POST /api/pipeline/trigger` with `specPath: forge/specs/approved/<slug>.json`).
- **Auth path**: Route any API calls through `withUserClient`/standard auth headers. If a bearer token is present but rejected, surface `401 AUTH_ERROR` — do not fall through to LOCAL_ADMIN.
- **Pulse timing**: Use a single shared `setInterval(500ms)` toggling `●`/`○` for all running rows; clear on `Esc`/unmount to avoid leaked timers. Distinguish `running` (green ●) vs `queued` (amber ○ + position) per existing kanban semantics.
- **Refresh cadence**: 5s poll must coexist with the pulse interval — separate timers, both cleared on unmount. Avoid duplicate polling on the same endpoint (prior 429 rate-limit storm bug in Runs panel).
- **Column layout**: Map three columns to existing kanban groupings — PENDING=draft, APPROVED=inProgress without active run, RUNNING/DONE=inProgress with activeRunStatus + done. Truncate slug to 28 chars with ellipsis; right-pad cards for clean `│` alignment in monospace.
- **Empty + overflow states**: Render placeholder `(empty)` row when a column has zero specs (acceptance: no crash when all empty). Show `+N more` only when `specs.length > 8`; never slice silently.
- **Keybindings hygiene**: Arrow nav must clamp to column bounds and skip empty columns. `r` only enabled on APPROVED column; `a` only on PENDING. After `a` succeeds, optimistically move card and trigger immediate refetch (don't wait for 5s tick). `Esc` must restore prior viewport state (board is overlay, not destructive).
- **Tailwind only**: Use monospace font class (`font-mono`) and Tailwind utilities for spacing/colors — no inline styles, no custom CSS.

userStories.title: Pi RPC session forking — clean slate per story with context preservation on retry
userStories.description:
Because pi runs as a warm RPC server (one process per spec run), session management uses RPC commands instead of CLI flags.

**Per-story clean slate** (already in CLI-004 via `new_session` command): each story starts with a fresh session. The warm server preserves the indexed codebase in memory (no cold start), but the conversation history is clean.

**Retry with context fork**: When a story fails and is retried (retry count > 0, agent = pi), instead of `new_session`, send a `clone` command to pi. This clones the current active session branch — the failing story's conversation history is preserved as context for the retry attempt, so the agent can learn from its previous error. The fork gives the agent the full failure context without re-indexing the codebase.

**Implementation in `spawnPiRpc()`**: Add an optional `retryContext?: { isRetry: boolean; attempt: number }` parameter. When `retryContext.isRetry === true`, send `{ type: 'clone' }` instead of `{ type: 'new_session' }` before sending the prompt.

**Session ID tracking**: After `new_session` or `clone`, call `{ type: 'get_state' }` and capture `state.sessionId`. Store this in `AgentResult` as `piSessionId?: string`. The WAL `story_started` event payload already accepts arbitrary metadata — add `piSessionId` there for observability.

**RpcCommand reference** (from pi's open-source rpc-types.ts):
- `{ type: 'new_session' }` → response: `{ success: true, data: { cancelled: boolean } }`
- `{ type: 'clone' }` → response: `{ success: true, data: { cancelled: boolean } }`
- `{ type: 'get_state' }` → response: `{ success: true, data: RpcSessionState }` where `state.sessionId` is the UUID

## Context
- Modify `spawnPiRpc()` in `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts` — this is the sole execution engine for all agent types; never touch `forge/run-loop.sh` (deprecated bash fallback).
- Reuse the existing `failureRegistry: Map<string, FailureRecord>` (from CP-002) to determine retry state — `getFailureRecord(storyId)?.recoveryAttempts` is the canonical retry counter, do NOT introduce a parallel counter.
- WAL events are emitted via `fetch` to `/api/wal` — extend the `story_started` payload with `piSessionId`; the WAL Zod schema uses `.nullish()` (not `.optional()`) for nullable fields, so type `piSessionId` accordingly when threading through.
- Capture `piSessionId` in `AgentResult` interface and propagate to the WAL emit call site; keep the field optional so non-pi agents (claude/opencode/codex) compile cleanly with no regression.
- Send RPC commands sequentially: `new_session` OR `clone` → await `{ success: true }` → `get_state` → capture `data.sessionId` → send prompt. Do not send the prompt before `get_state` resolves, or sessionId will be missing from the WAL.
- Gotcha: a `clone` on attempt 0 (first run, no prior session) will fail — guard with `retryContext?.isRetry === true && retryContext.attempt > 0`; first attempt always uses `new_session`.
- Test the 3-attempt retry assertion (1 new_session + 2 clones → 3 distinct UUIDs) by mocking the RPC transport, not by spawning a real pi server; backend tests run under Jest.
- Run `cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit` after changes — strict mode is enforced and `@ts-ignore` requires an inline justification comment per project standards.

userStories.title: Pi MCP bridge: mount Rorca's MCP tools inside pi interactive sessions
userStories.description:
Pi has native MCP support — it can connect to MCP servers and use their tools natively in interactive sessions. When `rorca chat` or any pi interactive session is launched, mount Rorca's own MCP server as a tool source. Implementation: (1) The Rorca backend already exposes an MCP HTTP endpoint (check backend/src/mcp/ and server.ts for the MCP transport). Get the MCP server URL — likely `http://localhost:3030/mcp` or the stdio server path. (2) Extend `rorca chat` (CLI-028) to pass the MCP connection to pi. Pi supports MCP via `--mcp-server <url>` or a config file (check pi's README/CLI help for the exact flag). If pi supports `--mcp-server http://localhost:3030/mcp`, append that flag. (3) When the MCP bridge connects, pi gains access to all ~400 Rorca MCP tools natively: `rorca_list_specs`, `rorca_generate_spec`, `rorca_trigger_run`, `rorca_get_memories`, etc. (4) Add a check to `rorca doctor` (CLI-024): verify MCP bridge connectivity by calling GET /api/health and checking the MCP status. If bridge not connectable: print `⚠ Rorca MCP bridge not connected — pi will run without Rorca tools`. (5) Document the MCP bridge URL in CLAUDE.md. Note: if pi uses a config file for MCP rather than a CLI flag, write the config file before spawning pi and clean it up after.

## Context
- **MCP server location**: Backend exposes MCP at `http://localhost:3030/mcp` (HTTP transport, API-first via OpenAPI auto-generation). Stdio fallback at `backend/src/mcp/server.ts` (24 hand-written tools). Check `backend/src/server.ts` for transport mount and `RORCA_SERVE_MCP` env flag handling.
- **Pi MCP flag discovery**: Run `pi --help` and check pi's README before assuming `--mcp-server` exists. If pi requires a config file (e.g. `~/.pi/mcp.json`), write to a temp path, pass via env/flag, and clean up in a `finally` block — never leave orphaned config on user's filesystem.
- **Doctor health check**: `GET /api/health` returns `{ opencodeInstalled, codexInstalled, ... }` — extend it (or add `/api/mcp/health`) to report MCP transport status. Distinguish three states: server not running (connection refused), server running but MCP disabled (`RORCA_SERVE_MCP=false`), and bridge healthy.
- **Backend must be live**: Pi MCP bridge requires the Express server on :3030. `rorca chat` should fail fast with actionable error ("start `npm run dev` or `rorca start` first") rather than spawning pi without tools silently.
- **No CLAUDE_BIN-style PATH gotchas**: Pi spawned as child process won't inherit NVM PATH — use absolute path resolution for `pi` binary (mirror the `CLAUDE_BIN`/`OPENCODE_BIN`/`CODEX_BIN` detector pattern in `backend/src/lib/`).

userStories.title: DB Strategy Orchestrator — Native PG default, Docker opt-in (Strategy C)
userStories.description:
Implement the hybrid DB strategy: Native Postgres is the default (preserves the one-command install), Docker sidecar with Apache AGE is opt-in for users who want graph memory. The existing `bin/rorca.ts` already implements native PG download from Maven Central (zonky.io binaries) to `~/.rorca/postgres/`. This story keeps that path AND adds an opt-in Docker path.

**Step 1 — Add `backend/src/lib/db-strategy.ts`** that exports:
- `type DbMode = 'native' | 'docker' | 'byop'` — Bring Your Own Postgres (BYOP) is when user sets DATABASE_URL to an external host
- `detectDbMode(): DbMode` — checks env in this order: `DATABASE_URL` set and host !== 'localhost'/'127.0.0.1' → 'byop'; `~/.rorca/db-mode` file contains 'docker' → 'docker'; default → 'native'
- `setDbMode(mode: DbMode): void` — writes `~/.rorca/db-mode` file (single line, chmod 0600)
- `getDbConnectionString(mode: DbMode): string` — native: `postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca`; docker: `postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5432/rorca`; byop: `process.env.DATABASE_URL`

**Step 2 — Add `backend/src/lib/db-sidecar.ts`** (Docker mode only) exporting:
- `dbStart(): Promise<void>` — runs `docker info` (3s timeout). If Docker not running, throw `{ code: 'DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE', hint: '...' }`. Inspects `rorca-db` container; starts if stopped, creates if missing: `docker run -d --name rorca-db -p 5432:5432 -v rorca-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data -e POSTGRES_DB=rorca -e POSTGRES_USER=rorca -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=rorca apache/age:latest`. Polls `docker exec rorca-db pg_isready -U rorca` every 1s up to 15s.
- `dbStop(): Promise<void>` — `docker stop rorca-db`.
- `dbStatus(): Promise<{ running: boolean; containerExists: boolean; ageEnabled: boolean }>` — never throws.
- `dbReset(): Promise<void>` — confirmation prompt (y/N), `docker rm -f rorca-db`, `docker volume rm rorca-db-data`, then `dbStart()`.
- `dbLogs(tail: number = 50): Promise<void>` — `docker logs --tail <n> --follow rorca-db` with stdio:inherit.
- `enableAgeExtension(): Promise<void>` — `docker exec rorca-db psql -U rorca -d rorca -c 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS age; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;'`

**Step 3 — Wire into existing `bin/rorca.ts`**. The existing file has `ensurePostgres()` for native mode. Add a branch at the top of `runStart()`:
```typescript
const mode = detectDbMode();
if (mode === 'docker') { await dbStart(); }
else if (mode === 'native') { await ensurePostgres(); /* existing code */ }
else { /* byop — assume DATABASE_URL is reachable, just run a connection probe */ }
```

**Step 4 — Backend graceful degradation**. The existing `pg-index.ts` already marks AGE migrations as non-fatal in `EXTENSION_MIGRATION_PATTERNS`. In native mode, AGE never loads. Add a helper `isAgeAvailable(): Promise<boolean>` to `backend/src/lib/db-strategy.ts` that runs `SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'age'` — returns false in native mode, true in docker mode after `enableAgeExtension()`.

**Important — preserve native PG path**: This story does NOT delete `bin/rorca.ts` `ensurePostgres()`. Native is the default. Docker is the upgrade path that unlocks graph memory. Most users never need to run `rorca db start`.

## Context
- **Native PG path is sacrosanct**: `bin/rorca.ts` `ensurePostgres()` downloads zonky.io PG to `~/.rorca/postgres/` on port 5433 — do NOT modify this code path. Add the `detectDbMode()` branch ABOVE the existing `ensurePostgres()` call in `runStart()`, leaving the native branch byte-for-byte intact.
- **Port discipline**: Native uses 5433 (existing `MANAGED_PG_PORT` constant), Docker uses 5432 (standard). Verify `MANAGED_PG_PORT` location in `bin/rorca.ts` and reference it from `getDbConnectionString('native')` rather than hardcoding — single source of truth.
- **AGE search_path poisoning still applies**: After `enableAgeExtension()`, any code calling `LOAD 'age'` or `setupAgeSession()` MUST restore `SET search_path = rorca, public` before releasing pool connections (see `db/index.ts` `on('connect')` safety net + memory `age_search_path_poison.md`). `isAgeAvailable()` itself is a simple `SELECT FROM pg_extension` — safe, no session mutation.
- **File permissions**: `~/.rorca/db-mode` must be `chmod 0600` (owner read/write only) — use `fs.writeFileSync(path, mode, { mode: 0o600 })` and verify on existing files via `fs.chmodSync` on every `setDbMode()` call (handles legacy files created without mode).
- **Docker detection timeout**: `docker info` 3s timeout is critical — Docker Desktop on macOS can hang indefinitely if the daemon is wedged. Use `child_process.spawn` with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)`, not `execSync`. Throw `{ code: 'DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE', hint: 'Install Docker Desktop or run `rorca db use native`' }`.
- **Idempotency for `dbStart()`**: Use `docker inspect rorca-db --format '{{.State.Running}}'` to distinguish missing/stopped/running. Missing → `docker run`; stopped → `docker start rorca-db`; running → no-op. Always poll `pg_isready` before returning (15s cap, 1s interval).
- **BYOP connection probe**: For `mode === 'byop'`, do a lightweight `SELECT 1` via the pg pool with a 5s connect timeout before proceeding. Surface user-friendly error (per engineering principles — never expose stack traces) if unreachable.
- **No new migrations needed**: AGE extension is created via `docker exec ... psql -c 'CREATE EXTENSION'`, NOT a migration file. Existing AGE migrations in `pg-migrations/` are already marked non-fatal via `EXTENSION_MIGRATION_PATTERNS` — no changes there.
- **Test gotcha**: Unit tests must mock `child_process.spawn` for docker calls and `fs` for `~/.rorca/db-mode`. Do NOT shell out to real docker in CI — gate integration tests behind `RORCA_DOCKER_TESTS=1`.
- **Strict TS + clean code**: All exports typed (no implicit any), functions under 40 lines. `dbStatus()` MUST never throw — wrap every docker call in try/catch and return `{ running: false, containerExists: false, ageEnabled: false }` on any error.

- `class Supervisor` with methods:
  - `spawn(name, cmd, args, env): SupervisedChild` — forks child, registers exit handler
  - `start(): Promise<void>` — spawns API child first, waits for `GET /api/health` to return 200 (poll 200ms up to 10s), then spawns Worker child
  - `stop(): Promise<void>` — sends SIGTERM to all children in reverse order (Worker first, then API), waits 30s drain, escalates to SIGKILL
  - `restartChild(name): void` — exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, capped at 30s. Max 5 restarts in 60s window → declare unhealthy, exit 1

**Step 2 — Update `cli.js` `runStart()`** to use Supervisor:
```javascript
import { Supervisor } from './backend/dist/lib/supervisor.js';
const sup = new Supervisor();
sup.spawn('api', 'node', ['backend/dist/server.js'], { ...env, RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE: 'api' });
await sup.waitForHealthy('http://localhost:3030/api/health', 10000);
sup.spawn('worker', 'node', ['backend/dist/worker.js'], { ...env, RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE: 'worker' });
process.on('SIGTERM', () => sup.stop());
process.on('SIGINT', () => sup.stop());
```

**Step 3 — Output multiplexing**. Both children's stdout/stderr is prefixed with `[api]` or `[worker]` and forwarded to the supervisor's stdout. Use a simple line-buffered prefix; ANSI codes pass through untouched.

**Step 4 — Worker not running detection**. The existing `GET /api/pipeline/worker/health` endpoint reads `worker_heartbeat` table. Supervisor's restart-on-crash path covers process death; but if the Worker process is alive but DB connection is dead, heartbeats stop. Add a 60s tick in supervisor that checks `last_seen` on `worker_heartbeat`; if stale > 90s, send SIGKILL to Worker child (forces restart via supervisor).

**Step 5 — Scheduler stays in API**. Confirm `backend/src/lib/scheduler.ts` is started inside `backend/src/server.ts` (it already is via `startScheduler()` call). No code move needed. Add a comment: `// Scheduler runs in-process with API — see CLI-035 Supervisor decision.`

**Important constraint**: The Worker process MUST NOT spawn nested workers. The existing `RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE=engine` env var prevents this for execution-engine subprocesses; add `RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE=worker` to suppress any startup logic that would fork a worker from within the worker process itself.

## Context
- **Use existing patterns from `backend/src/worker.ts` and `backend/src/server.ts`** — both already handle `SIGTERM` for graceful shutdown (worker drains in-flight jobs up to 30s). Mirror this drain behavior in the Supervisor's stop sequence; do not reinvent signal handling.
- **`RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE` is already a load-bearing env var** — `engine` is set by the worker when spawning execution-engine subprocesses to prevent nested workers. Adding `worker` and `api` values means any code that branches on this var (grep for `RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE` before adding) must handle the new values explicitly, not fall through.
- **`worker_heartbeat` schema reminder** — columns are `(worker_id, pid, hostname, started_at, last_seen)` with `last_seen` updated every 30s; stale threshold is `> 90s` (matches existing `GET /api/pipeline/worker/health` logic). Reuse that query, do not duplicate the staleness constant.
- **Health poll endpoint contract** — `GET /api/health` returns 200 once Express is listening AND DB pool is reachable. Poll at 200ms intervals up to 10s as specified; on timeout, kill the API child and exit 1 (do NOT spawn the Worker against a broken API).
- **CLI imports compiled JS, not tsx** — `cli.js` is the npm-installed entry point and must import from `backend/dist/`, not `backend/src/`. Ensure `supervisor.ts` is included in the `tsc` build output and exported from `backend/dist/lib/supervisor.js`.
- **Output multiplexing gotcha** — `claude --print --output-format stream-json` writes diagnostic JSON to stderr (see Notable Bug Fix 2026-03-17). Prefix wrapping for `[worker]` stderr should NOT attempt to parse or filter — pass bytes through line-buffered, ANSI intact. The execution-engine already handles JSON filtering downstream.
- **Restart loop must not mask startup bugs** — exponential backoff (1/2/4/8/30s, max 5 in 60s → exit 1) is critical; without the cap, a crash-looping Worker would spam `pipeline_runs` rows and pg-boss state. Log every restart with `(name, restartCount, exitCode, signal)` for postmortem.
- **Reverse-order shutdown is non-negotiable** — Worker must SIGTERM first so in-flight pg-boss jobs complete and write `story_results` before the API (which serves `/api/wal` and `/api/pipeline/story-result`) goes down. Reversing this order causes silent story-result loss.
- **Do NOT add tsx watch anywhere in the supervisor path** — see `feedback_tsx_watch.md`. Production `rorca start` uses plain `node backend/dist/*.js`; restarts must be supervisor-driven, not file-watcher-driven.
- **Test the end-to-end fix manually** — after implementation, `npm pack && npm i -g ./rorca-*.tgz && rorca start` then trigger a pipeline run via UI; confirm Worker picks it up within ~500ms (pg-boss polling interval). The acceptance criterion "queued pipeline run executes end-to-end" requires this verification, not just unit tests.

userStories.title: Bundle Manifest — verify npm pack ships dist/ + backend/dist/, no build on user machine
userStories.description:
Today's `npm install -g rorca` will FAIL for non-developers because the published tarball assumes `dist/` (frontend) and `backend/dist/` (compiled TS) exist locally — but they're built only when devs run `npm run build`. The `prepublishOnly` script runs build before publish, but `npm pack --dry-run` today shows the tarball is empty unless `dist/` already exists locally.

**Step 1 — Verify prepublishOnly runs build**. Existing `package.json`:
```json
"prepublishOnly": "npm run build",
"build": "vite build && cd backend && tsc && cd .. && npx tsc --project bin/tsconfig.json"
```
This is correct in theory but never tested. Add a CI step that runs `npm pack` in a clean clone (no prior `npm run build`) and verifies the tarball contains:
- `dist/index.html` (frontend entry)
- `dist/assets/*.js` (frontend bundles)
- `backend/dist/server.js` (compiled API)
- `backend/dist/worker.js` (compiled worker)
- `backend/dist/lib/supervisor.js` (from CLI-035)
- `backend/src/db/migrations/*.sql` (migrations — these ship as source)
- `bin/rorca.js` (compiled CLI)
- `cli.js` (entry point)

**Step 2 — Add `scripts/verify-pack.sh`**:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
git clean -fdx -e .env.local  # nuke local builds
npm install
npm pack --pack-destination="$TMPDIR"
TARBALL=$(ls "$TMPDIR"/rorca-*.tgz)
echo "Tarball: $TARBALL ($(du -h $TARBALL | cut -f1))"
tar tzf "$TARBALL" | sort > "$TMPDIR/contents.txt"
for required in 'package/dist/index.html' 'package/backend/dist/server.js' 'package/backend/dist/worker.js' 'package/cli.js' 'package/bin/rorca.js'; do
  grep -qx "$required" "$TMPDIR/contents.txt" || { echo "✗ MISSING: $required"; exit 1; }
done
echo "✓ All required artifacts present"
# Smoke install in clean env
INSTALL_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
cd "$INSTALL_DIR" && npm install --prefix . "$TARBALL" >/dev/null
test -x ./node_modules/.bin/rorca || { echo "✗ rorca binary not executable after install"; exit 1; }
echo "✓ Smoke install passed"
```
Make executable: `chmod +x scripts/verify-pack.sh`.

**Step 3 — Wire into CI**. Add to `.github/workflows/release.yml` (create if missing):
```yaml
- name: Verify pack
  run: ./scripts/verify-pack.sh
```

**Step 4 — Tighten root package.json `files` field** to be explicit (current list is mostly correct):
```json
"files": [
  "bin/rorca.js",
  "bin/rorca.d.ts",
  "cli.js",
  "dist/",
  "backend/dist/",
  "backend/src/db/migrations/",
  "backend/src/db/pg-migrations/",
  "backend/package.json",
  "backend/package-lock.json",
  "forge/run-loop.sh",
  "forge/self-register.ts",
  "package.json",
  "README.md",
  "LICENSE"
]
```
Notably missing currently: `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/` (the migrations the runner needs at runtime). README and LICENSE for npm display.

**Step 5 — Add explicit exclude for packages/**. Without this, `packages/rorca-cli/` from CLI-034 might leak into the tarball:
```json
"files": [...]  // packages/ NOT listed = excluded by default with files field
```
Verify in `scripts/verify-pack.sh` that `packages/` does NOT appear in tarball contents.

## Context
- Bundle ships PostgreSQL migrations from `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/` (NOT `backend/src/db/migrations/` — that path in the story description is wrong); `pg-index.ts` runs them at startup, so they're load-bearing at runtime

- `node-pty` is a native module that CANNOT be bundled — tarball must NOT include `backend/node_modules/node-pty/prebuilds/` (platform-specific); users run `npm rebuild node-pty` post-install (graceful 503 fallback already in `pty-manager.ts`)
- CLI-035 supervisor (`backend/dist/lib/supervisor.js`) is a build artifact — confirm `tsc` in backend produces it before tarball assembly; missing supervisor breaks `rorca start`

- `git clean -fdx` in verify script will nuke `.env.local`, `node_modules/`, and any local Postgres data — the `-e .env.local` exclusion is critical; double-check no other dev-only files need preserving (`.rorca/`, `~/.rorca/postgres/` is outside repo so safe)

userStories.title: rorca doctor v2 — Docker, pi, ports, AGE, migrations, version match, worker heartbeat
userStories.description:
Expand `rorca doctor` (CLI-024) into a comprehensive health check suite. Each check has: name, status (✓/⚠/✗), detail message, and optional fix hint. The original CLI-024 is the V0 baseline; this story adds checks introduced by CLI-033 → CLI-037 + CLI-044.

**Check sequence** (in order — later checks depend on earlier passing):
1. **Node version** (≥20.0.0) — from process.version
2. **Pi binary** — calls detectPi(); ⚠ if missing, hint to run `rorca auth login` (which triggers install in CLI-040)
3. **Pi version** — must be ≥ MIN_PI_VERSION constant (set to '0.67.0' for V0)
4. **DB mode** — calls detectDbMode(); displays 'native' / 'docker' / 'byop' as info
5. **Native PG** (only if mode=native) — checks ~/.rorca/postgres/ exists, port 5433 reachable
6. **Docker daemon** (only if mode=docker) — `docker info` 3s timeout
7. **DB container** (only if mode=docker) — calls dbStatus(); ✗ if not running, hint to run `rorca db start`
8. **AGE extension** (only if mode=docker) — calls isAgeAvailable(); ⚠ if false (graph features disabled)
9. **Backend port** — :3030 reachable; ✗ if not, hint to run `rorca start`
10. **Backend version** — calls /api/version; ✗ on mismatch with CLI's MIN_BACKEND_VERSION
11. **Schema migrations** — current schemaVersion vs expected (count of files in pg-migrations/)
12. **Worker heartbeat** — `GET /api/pipeline/worker/health`; ⚠ if last_seen > 90s ago, ✗ if no heartbeat
13. **MCP bridge** (info only) — `GET /mcp` reachable, count tools
14. **Workspace files** — checks .rorca/config.json, MEMORY.md, AGENTS.md exist in cwd

**Output format** — table with fixed-width columns:
```
  ✓ Node version          v20.18.0
  ✓ Pi binary             /Users/x/.bun/bin/pi (v0.67.2)
  ✓ DB mode               native (default)
  ✓ Native PG             :5433 ready
  ✗ Backend port          :3030 unreachable
      → Run: rorca start
  ⚠ Worker heartbeat      stale 142s ago
      → Run: kill -SIGKILL <worker_pid> (supervisor restarts)
```

**Exit codes**:
- 0 — all checks pass
- 1 — one or more ✗ (critical failures)
- 2 — only ⚠ warnings, no failures

**Flags**:
- `--json` — machine-readable output for CI
- `--check <name>` — run single named check
- `--verbose` — show detail for ✓ checks too

## Context
- **Reuse existing detectors**: Import `detectPi()`, `detectDbMode()`, `dbStatus()`, `isAgeAvailable()`, and `checkVersion()` (CLI-036) from their existing modules — do not reimplement detection logic. Add `MIN_PI_VERSION = '0.67.0'` constant to `pi-detector.ts`.
- **Worker heartbeat semantics**: Query `GET /api/pipeline/worker/health` (not the `worker_heartbeat` table directly). Stale threshold is `last_seen > 90s` per CLAUDE.md gotcha #6 — match that exact value, don't invent a new one.
- **Schema migration count**: Read files from `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/` — both sequential (`001-079`) and timestamp (`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_*.sql`) formats coexist. Count all `.sql` files; compare against `schema_migrations` table version. Use `checkDuplicatePrefixes()` pattern from `pg-index.ts` if duplicate detection is needed.
- **Conditional check skipping**: When `mode=native`, skip Docker daemon + DB container + AGE checks entirely (don't render them as ✗). When `mode=docker`, skip the Native PG check. `--check <name>` flag bypasses the dependency ordering.
- **Backend-down resilience**: Checks 10–13 (backend version, migrations, worker heartbeat, MCP) all depend on :3030 being up. If check 9 (port) fails, mark dependents as `✗ skipped (backend down)` with a single fix hint pointing to check 9 — do not cascade duplicate hints.
- **Exit code precedence**: Any ✗ → exit 1 (overrides ⚠); ⚠-only → exit 2; all ✓ → exit 0. Compute after all checks complete, not short-circuit.
- **JSON output shape**: `{ checks: [{ name, status: 'pass'|'warn'|'fail', detail, hint? }], exitCode }` — use string statuses in JSON (not unicode symbols), keep symbols only for human TTY output.
- **Workspace files check uses `process.cwd()`**: Look for `.rorca/config.json`, `MEMORY.md`, `AGENTS.md` at workspace root per CLAUDE.md gotcha ("Workspace Context Files — Root Level Required") — NOT in subdirectories or `.rorca/MEMORY.md`.
- **Output formatting**: Fixed-width column alignment via padding (no external table lib needed). Fix hints indented with 6 spaces + `→` prefix. Keep functions under 40 lines per engineering standards — split per-check logic into small functions returning a typed `CheckResult`.

userStories.title: Pi Distribution: Detect + Prompt — guided install if pi binary missing
userStories.description:
If pi is not installed, `rorca init` and `rorca auth login` should offer to install it for the user rather than failing with 'pi not found'. We chose 'detect + prompt' over 'bundle' (avoids 50-100MB tarball bloat) and over 'auto-download' (preserves user agency).

**Step 1 — Detection in `rorca init` and `rorca auth login`**. Both commands call `detectPi()` from CLI-002. If `piInstalled === false`:

```
Pi binary not found.

Rorca uses pi (https://github.com/mariozechner/pi) as its execution engine.

Install pi now?
  [1] npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
  [2] pnpm add -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
  [3] bun add -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
  [4] curl -fsSL https://pi.mariozechner.com/install.sh | sh
  [5] Skip — I'll install it manually

Choice [1-5]:
```

**Step 2 — Auto-detect package manager**. Inspect `process.env.npm_config_user_agent` (set by npm/pnpm/bun) to highlight the matching option. If user is invoking via bun, default selection is [3]. Otherwise default to [1].

**Step 3 — Execute install**. For options 1-3, run via `execa(cmd, args, { stdio: 'inherit' })` so the user sees install progress. For option 4, prompt for confirmation: `Run curl install script from pi.mariozechner.com? [y/N]:` — only proceed on 'y'. Print the URL again so the user sees it before agreeing.

**Step 4 — Verify install succeeded**. After install command exits, re-run `detectPi()`. If still not found:
```
✗ Pi installation completed but binary not on PATH.

This usually means npm's global bin directory is not in your PATH.
Try:
  npm config get prefix
  echo 'export PATH="<prefix>/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
  source ~/.zshrc
```
Exit 1.

**Step 5 — `--auto-install-pi` flag**. For non-interactive contexts (CI, Dockerfile), accept this flag on `rorca init` to skip the prompt and run option [1] directly. Without the flag in non-TTY contexts, fall back to printing instructions and exit 1 (don't hang waiting for input that won't come).

**Step 6 — Document in README and CLAUDE.md**: pi is a peer dependency, not bundled. The 'detect + prompt' UX is the install bridge.

## Context
- **Reuse CLI-002 primitives**: Import `detectPi()` and `PI_INSTALL_METHODS` rather than duplicating detection logic or hardcoding install commands — single source of truth for install methods.
- **TTY detection before prompts**: Gate interactive prompts on `process.stdout.isTTY && process.stdin.isTTY`. Non-TTY without `--auto-install-pi` must exit 1 with instructions, never hang on `readline` waiting for stdin.
- **Package manager detection**: Parse `process.env.npm_config_user_agent` (format: `npm/10.2.4 node/v20.x` or `pnpm/8.x` or `bun/1.x`). Default to [1] (npm) when unset or unrecognized — don't crash on missing env var.
- **execa with stdio:inherit, not exec**: Use `execa(cmd, args, { stdio: 'inherit' })` so install progress streams live. Catch non-zero exit codes and surface them — do NOT swallow errors or fall through to verification on failed install.
- **Curl confirmation is mandatory**: Option [4] must re-print the full URL (`https://pi.mariozechner.com/install.sh`) and require explicit `y` (case-insensitive). Treat empty input, `n`, or anything else as decline. Security boundary — never auto-execute remote scripts.
- **PATH troubleshooting message must be actionable**: After failed re-detection, print the exact `npm config get prefix` + shell rc append commands. Detect user's shell from `process.env.SHELL` to pick `~/.zshrc` vs `~/.bashrc` vs `~/.config/fish/config.fish`.
- **Skip option [5] is non-fatal**: Print amber warning ("Runs will fail until pi is installed: <install URL>") and return success (exit 0) so `rorca init` can complete workspace setup. Only the actual run trigger should fail later.
- **Surface user-friendly errors**: Per engineering standards, never expose execa stderr stack traces directly — wrap in "Pi installation failed: <one-line summary>. See output above." Log full context (command, exit code, timestamp) for debugging.
- **CLAUDE.md update belongs in this story**: Add a "Pi peer dependency" subsection under Environment or Distribution, documenting the detect+prompt rationale (avoids 50-100MB bundle bloat, preserves user agency).

userStories.title: Lite-to-Full Migration — pg_dump from native to Docker for graph upgrade
userStories.description:
When a user starts in Lite Mode (native PG, no AGE) then later runs `rorca db start` to enable graph memory, their existing data must migrate from native :5433 to Docker :5432. Without this story, users lose their workspaces, specs, and runs on upgrade.

**Step 1 — Detect upgrade path in `rorca db start`**. Modified flow:
```
1. Check current DB mode (detectDbMode())
2. If mode === 'native':
   a. Confirm: 'Upgrade from Lite Mode (native) to Full Mode (Docker+AGE)?'
   b. Confirm again: 'This will copy ~XMB of data. Native DB will be stopped after migration. Continue? [y/N]'
   c. Run migration sequence (Steps 2-6 below)
3. If mode === 'docker': just start container (no migration needed)
4. If mode === 'byop': error — BYOP users manage their own DB
```

**Step 2 — Pre-flight checks**:
- Native PG running on :5433 (start it if stopped via existing ensurePostgres())
- Docker daemon available (docker info)
- Disk space available (du -sh ~/.rorca/postgres/ × 2)
- No active runs (check pipeline_runs WHERE status='running' = empty)

**Step 3 — Backup native data**:
```bash
pg_dump -h localhost -p 5433 -U rorca -d rorca -Fc -f ~/.rorca/migrations/lite-backup-<timestamp>.dump
```
Progress reported via dump size polling. If pg_dump fails, abort migration; native data untouched.

**Step 4 — Start Docker, prepare schema**:
```bash
dbStart()  # creates rorca-db container
enableAgeExtension()  # CREATE EXTENSION age, vector
```

**Step 5 — Restore data**:
```bash
pg_restore -h localhost -p 5432 -U rorca -d rorca --no-owner --no-acl ~/.rorca/migrations/lite-backup-<timestamp>.dump
```
Note `--no-owner --no-acl` because owner is 'rorca' on native but might differ in container env.

**Step 6 — Replay AGE-skipped migrations**. The native install marked AGE migrations as `applied=true` in `schema_migrations` to prevent crashes. Now that AGE is available, those migrations need to actually run:
```sql
UPDATE schema_migrations SET applied=false WHERE version IN (SELECT version FROM schema_migrations WHERE version IN (<known AGE migration list>));
```
Then restart backend (or run migration runner programmatically) to apply them. **Note**: This requires a small change to `pg-index.ts` to add a `skipped_in_lite_mode` column tracking which migrations were lite-skipped vs genuinely applied. See CLI-033 graceful degradation.

**Step 7 — Switch mode and verify**:
```bash
setDbMode('docker')
# Run smoke query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM workspaces
# Run AGE smoke query: SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.ag_graph LIMIT 1
```
If either fails, restore native mode (`setDbMode('native')`), keep both DBs running, print error.

**Step 8 — Stop native PG (preserve data dir)**. Native PG is stopped but `~/.rorca/postgres/data/` is left intact. User can downgrade back to native via `rorca db downgrade` (future story; out of scope here). Print: `✓ Migration complete. Native PG data preserved at ~/.rorca/postgres/data/. To roll back, set RORCA_DB_MODE=native and restart.`

**Step 9 — Idempotency**. Re-running `rorca db start` after successful upgrade does NOT re-migrate. Check `~/.rorca/db-mode === 'docker'` first; if so, just verify container is running.

## Context
- **Migration runner integration**: Add `skipped_in_lite_mode BOOLEAN DEFAULT false` column to `schema_migrations` via new timestamp-format migration (`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_add_skipped_in_lite_mode.sql`) — sequential format is reserved for 001-079. Update `backend/src/db/pg-index.ts` to set this flag when AGE migrations are skipped in Lite Mode, and clear it during upgrade replay.

- **AGE search_path hygiene applies post-upgrade**: After enabling AGE extension on Docker, any code path that runs `LOAD 'age'` or `setupAgeSession()` MUST restore `SET search_path = rorca, public` before releasing the connection (see knowledge-graph.ts, graph-context.ts pattern). The pool `on('connect')` safety net in `db/index.ts` is not a substitute. Failing to do so causes intermittent "Workspace not found" 404s.

- **Active run check must use pg-boss + pipeline_runs**: Pre-flight "no active runs" check should query both `pipeline_runs WHERE status IN ('running','queued')` AND verify pg-boss has no active jobs in `pgboss.job` — worker may have stale active jobs that survive restarts (see Worker stale jobs bug, 2026-03-13).

- **Backend restart required after migration replay**: `pg-index.ts` runs migrations on backend startup, not on demand. After updating `schema_migrations.applied=false`, either expose a programmatic `runPendingMigrations()` export OR signal the user to restart. Don't assume tsx watch reloads — the user has explicitly disabled tsx watch for the server (see feedback_tsx_watch.md).

- **Atomicity via mode flag, not transactions**: Cross-database migration cannot be wrapped in a single transaction. Use `~/.rorca/db-mode` as the source of truth — only flip to `'docker'` after all verifications pass. On failure, leave both DBs running so user can manually recover (matches no-shortcuts feedback rule — no silent rollback that loses data).

- **Connection pool reset required**: After `setDbMode('docker')`, the existing `pg.Pool` in `backend/src/db/index.ts` still points at :5433. Backend must be restarted OR pool must be torn down and recreated with new `DATABASE_URL`. Document this as a required restart step.

- **Disk space check must account for pg_dump compression**: `-Fc` (custom format) compresses ~3-5x. Estimate free space as `du -sh ~/.rorca/postgres/data` × 1.5 (not × 2) for the dump, plus full size again for Docker volume. Be explicit in the prompt about total required.

- **CLI lives in `bin/rorca.ts`**: This story modifies the `rorca db start` command — work in `bin/rorca.ts` (already in git status as modified). Use existing helpers `detectDbMode()`, `ensurePostgres()`, `dbStart()`, `setDbMode()` rather than reimplementing. Conventional commit prefix: `feat:`.

- **No auth context needed**: This is a CLI-level operation running as the local user against `~/.rorca/`. No `withUserClient()` or RLS concerns — pure infrastructure migration.

userStories.title: AEGIS P0 + OPEN-CORE: Curate the 4-tier Allow-list — public API contract, paid paywall, admin lockdown
userStories.description:
**SECURITY + COMMERCIAL CRITICAL.** With CLI-047's opt-IN gate in place, MCP currently exposes 0 tools. This story applies `x-rorca-tier` annotations to all ~414 backend routes, creating the canonical allow-list across all four tiers.

**The annotation is now the legal/commercial frontier**: `x-rorca-tier: public` routes become the **stable API contract** that the open-source CLI depends on. `x-rorca-tier: paid` routes become the **paywall boundary**. Once a route is annotated `public-api: true`, you cannot break it without a major version bump — external CLI consumers may be calling it.

**Target distribution** (~414 routes total):

| Tier | Count target | Marked publicApi | Examples |
|------|------|------|------|
| `public` | ~28 | ALL public-tier routes are publicApi=true | Spec CRUD, story exec, recall, search, health, direction read |
| `auth` | ~15 | NO (login-required, not part of stable open-source contract) | User profile, owned workspace settings |
| `paid` | ~25 | NO (paywall boundary) | Teams, federated memory, GRC traces, FinOps, marketplace publish |
| `admin` | ~10 | NO (single-user local) | Backups, license gen, embed-all, graph-backfill |
| (denied) | ~336 | NO | All terminal, vault writes, skill installs, webhooks, etc. |

**Public tier (~28 routes, x-rorca-tier: public, x-rorca-public-api: true)** — open-source CLI surface, MCP-exposed, stable contract:
- **Specs (read)**: `GET /api/specs`, `GET /api/specs/{specId}`, `GET /api/specs/archive`, `GET /api/specs/kanban`, `GET /api/specs/{specId}/versions`, `GET /api/specs/{specId}/diff`, `GET /api/specs/{specId}/graph`, `GET /api/specs/search-stories`
- **Specs (mutate)**: `POST /api/specs/generate`, `POST /api/specs/{specId}/approve`, `POST /api/specs/{specId}/reject`, `POST /api/specs/{specId}/add-stories`, `PUT /api/specs/{specId}`, `PATCH /api/specs/{specId}/stories/{storyId}`, `DELETE /api/specs/{specId}/stories/{storyId}`
- **Pipeline**: `GET /api/pipeline/runs`, `GET /api/pipeline/runs/{runId}`, `GET /api/pipeline/runs/{runId}/log`, `POST /api/pipeline/trigger`, `POST /api/pipeline/runs/{runId}/cancel`, `POST /api/pipeline/runs/{runId}/retry`
- **Direction (single-user)**: `GET /api/direction`, `GET /api/direction/synthesize`, `PUT /api/direction`
- **Memory (local-only)**: `GET /api/memory`, `GET /api/recall`, `POST /api/memory`, `PUT /api/memory/entry`
- **Search**: `GET /api/search`, `GET /api/stories/search`
- **Health**: `GET /api/health`, `GET /api/version`

**Auth tier (~15 routes, x-rorca-tier: auth)** — logged-in users only, MCP-exposed only with auth token, NOT part of open-source stable contract:
- `GET /api/users/me`, `GET /api/settings/profile`, `GET /api/settings/display`, `PUT /api/settings/profile`, `PUT /api/settings/display`
- `GET /api/workspaces`, `GET /api/workspaces/{id}` (own workspaces), `PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}`
- `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/health`, `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/stats`
- `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/rorca-config`, `PUT /api/workspaces/{id}/rorca-config`
- `GET /api/onboarding`, `PUT /api/onboarding`

**Paid tier (~25 routes, x-rorca-tier: paid)** — license/subscription required, NEVER MCP-exposed, returns 402 PLAN_REQUIRED on free plan:
- **Teams + RBAC**: `GET /api/teams`, `POST /api/teams`, `GET /api/teams/{id}/members`, `POST /api/teams/{id}/members`, `DELETE /api/teams/{id}/members/{userId}`, `PATCH /api/teams/{id}/members/{userId}`, `GET /api/teams/{id}/invites`, `POST /api/invites`
- **Federated Memory**: `GET /api/memory/cross-workspace/{workspaceId}`, `POST /api/memory/cross-workspace/{workspaceId}/accept/{entryId}`, `DELETE /api/memory/cross-workspace/{workspaceId}/dismiss/{entryId}`
- **GRC / Audit**: `GET /api/admin/mcp-audit` (the audit log itself, paid tier), `GET /api/integrations/audit-log`
- **FinOps**: `GET /api/analytics/finops-export`, `GET /api/analytics/finops-historical`, `GET /api/analytics/roi`, `GET /api/analytics/roi-config`, `GET /api/analytics/pi-providers` (CLI-030)
- **Marketplace publish**: `POST /api/marketplace/publish`, `POST /api/marketplace/{id}/fork`
- **Cloud sync** (placeholder for future): `GET /api/sync/status`, `POST /api/sync/push`, `POST /api/sync/pull`

**Admin tier (~10 routes, x-rorca-tier: admin)** — single-user local admin, NEVER MCP-exposed, NEVER open-source-CLI accessible:
- `POST /api/admin/backup`, `GET /api/admin/backups`, `POST /api/admin/embed-all`, `GET /api/admin/embed-all/status`, `PUT /api/admin/embedding-provider`, `POST /api/admin/generate-license`, `POST /api/admin/graph-backfill`, `GET /api/admin/graph-stats`

**Denied (default — ~336 routes, no annotation)** — never MCP-exposed, never CLI-accessible:
- All `/api/vault/*` (encrypted credential operations)
- All `/api/terminal/*` (PTY spawn, shell exec)
- All `/api/workspaces/{id}/env-vars` (env injection vector)
- All `/api/skills/install*` (prompt injection vector)
- All `/api/webhooks/*` and `/api/billing/webhook` (signature spoofing)
- All `/api/auth/*` (JWT operations — handled via cookie auth, not API)
- All `/api/copilot/*` (third-party OAuth tokens)
- All `/api/integrations/*` mutations
- `POST /api/workspaces` (filesystem read enabler — admin tier handles workspace creation safely via UI)
- All other `DELETE` routes except scoped story/comment deletes
- All internal/diagnostic routes

**Step 1 — Apply annotations**. For each ~80 annotated routes, add `x-rorca-tier`, `x-rorca-rationale`, and (for public tier) `x-rorca-public-api: true`. Each rationale must justify exposure for that specific tier.

**Step 2 — Verify lint output**:
```
[Tier Lint] Tier exposure: 28 public, 15 auth, 25 paid, 10 admin (336 default-denied)
[Tier Lint] Open-source CLI public API surface: 28 routes
[Tier Lint] MCP-exposed (public + auth): 43 tools
```

**Step 3 — Smoke tests**:
```bash
# As open-source CLI (public token, no plan)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $PUBLIC_TOKEN" /api/specs        # 200
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $PUBLIC_TOKEN" /api/teams        # 402 PLAN_REQUIRED
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $PUBLIC_TOKEN" /api/admin/backup # 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED

# As paid user (web UI cookie, plan='pro')
GET /api/teams                                                  # 200

# As MCP client (admin token)
MCP list-tools → returns ~43 (public + auth), NOT teams/admin
```

**Step 4 — Generate `OPEN_API_CONTRACT.md`**: lint script generates a markdown file at `docs/OPEN_API_CONTRACT.md` listing every public-tier + public-api route with its method/path/parameters. This becomes the **legal contract** for the open-source CLI — these routes have stable URLs and request/response shapes.

**Step 5 — Adversarial review**. After annotations applied, paranoid pass with three threat actors:
- **Drive-by browser** (origin attacker): Can the public/auth tier routes be abused?
- **Forked CLI** (commercial competitor running modified CLI): Can paid features be reached by hitting paid endpoints with public token?
- **MCP agent** (LLM with admin token): Can it accidentally trigger billing/admin operations?

If any of these answer YES, REMOVE the route from its tier or fix the gating.

**Step 6 — Update stdio MCP server** at `backend/src/mcp/server.ts` to mirror the public+auth tier. The 24 hand-written tools become the public-tier subset.

## Context
- **Tier annotations live in @swagger JSDoc**: Add `x-rorca-tier`, `x-rorca-rationale`, and `x-rorca-public-api` as custom OpenAPI extensions in the `@swagger` blocks above each route handler in `backend/src/routes/*.ts`. These flow through `backend/src/lib/swagger.ts` into the OpenAPI spec, which is the single source of truth for both REST docs and MCP tool generation (API-first architecture).
- **MCP exposure gating is in `backend/src/mcp/server.ts`**: The stdio server currently has 24 hand-written tools — must be pruned/aligned to the public+auth subset (~43). Do NOT add paid/admin tools here. The HTTP MCP transport (auto-generated from OpenAPI) must filter by `x-rorca-tier in {public, auth}` only.
- **Default-deny is the security posture**: Per CLI-047's opt-IN gate, missing annotation = denied. Do NOT annotate routes you're unsure about — leaving them unannotated is the correct safe default. The ~336 unannotated routes is a feature, not a gap.
- **Vault/terminal/skills-install/webhooks/auth/copilot/env-vars MUST stay unannotated**: These are prompt-injection or credential-exfiltration vectors. Even `auth` tier exposes them to MCP via auth token — never safe. Verify with grep before lint runs.
- **`POST /api/workspaces` is denied, not admin**: It's a filesystem-read enabler (path traversal, arbitrary directory registration). Workspace creation flows through UI only; admin tier covers backup/license/embed operations, not workspace registration.
- **`public-api: true` is a legal contract, not a convenience flag**: Once shipped, the route's URL + request/response shape cannot change without major version bump. Lint must fail if any non-public tier carries `public-api: true`. Be conservative: prefer annotating fewer public routes than risk locking in an unstable contract.
- **402 PLAN_REQUIRED vs 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED are distinct error codes**: Paid tier returns 402 (use `AppError` subclass — likely needs new `PaymentRequiredError` in `backend/src/lib/errors.ts`). Admin returns 403 `ForbiddenError`. Public token hitting paid → 402; public token hitting admin → 403.
- **Adversarial review must check the stdio server too**: The forked-CLI threat actor can `npx tsx backend/src/mcp/server.ts` directly — ensure no paid/admin logic leaks via the hand-written tool implementations bypassing the tier check. The stdio tool list is the second enforcement boundary.
- **`docs/OPEN_API_CONTRACT.md` should be regenerated, not hand-edited**: Create a script (e.g., `scripts/generate-api-contract.ts`) that reads the OpenAPI JSON and emits the markdown. Add to `npm run lint:tier` so contract drift is caught in CI.

userStories.title: AEGIS P0: Remove No-op OAuth Theater — honest auth model
userStories.description:
**SECURITY CRITICAL.** Lines 277-331 of backend/src/server.ts implement a fake OAuth 2.0 flow that auto-approves any client and issues a static token (`'rorca-local-access-token'`) which is **never validated**. The comment explicitly states: *'Trivial local OAuth 2.0 server — no real security, just satisfies the protocol.'*

This fake OAuth is dangerous in two ways:
1. **Misleads code reviewers** into believing auth exists where it doesn't
2. **Conflicts with CLI-045 Bearer auth** — token endpoint hands out tokens that bypass the new check (if mcpHandlers don't enforce token validity, the OAuth-issued token works)

**Step 1 — Delete OAuth handlers**. Remove from `backend/src/server.ts`:
- `app.get('/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server', ...)` (lines 282-292)
- `app.get('/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource', ...)` (lines 293-298)
- `handleOAuthRegister` const + `app.post('/oauth/register', ...)` + `app.post('/register', ...)` (lines 299-313)
- `app.get('/oauth/authorize', ...)` (lines 314-322)
- `app.post('/oauth/token', ...)` (lines 323-331)
- The `MCP_OAUTH_BASE` constant (line 281)

**Step 2 — Replace with honest 501 responses** so MCP clients that probe OAuth endpoints get clear feedback:
```typescript
const NO_OAUTH_RESPONSE = {
  error: 'OAuth not supported',
  message: 'Rorca uses Bearer token authentication, not OAuth. See ~/.rorca/mcp-token.',
  documentation: 'Run `rorca mcp setup-claude` to configure your MCP client.',
};
for (const path of ['/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server', '/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource', '/oauth/authorize', '/oauth/token', '/oauth/register', '/register']) {
  app.all(path, (_req, res) => res.status(501).json(NO_OAUTH_RESPONSE));
}
```

**Step 3 — Claude Desktop compatibility note**. Newer Claude Desktop versions strictly require OAuth for MCP HTTP servers. Without real OAuth, those versions cannot connect. Two options:

**Option A (chosen for V0)**: Document the limitation. Users connect via Claude Code CLI (`claude mcp add ... --header 'Authorization: Bearer ...'`) or VS Code extension instead. Claude Desktop integration deferred until either (a) Claude Desktop adds Bearer support, or (b) we implement real OAuth in a future story.

**Option B (deferred)**: Implement real OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. This is significant work (real authorization codes, real token validation, refresh token storage, scope enforcement). Punt to v1.x post-launch.

**Step 4 — README and CLAUDE.md updates**:
- Add Security section explaining: "Rorca uses Bearer token auth at /mcp. The previous trivial OAuth implementation has been removed for honesty — it provided no security and misled code readers."
- Connection examples for Claude Code CLI, VS Code extension, custom integrations
- Note about Claude Desktop limitation + workaround (use Claude Code CLI instead)

**Step 5 — Migration script** for existing users who configured Claude Desktop with the no-op OAuth: `rorca mcp diagnose-clients` scans for known MCP client config files (Claude Desktop config.json, VS Code settings) and prints which ones will break, with fix instructions per client.

## Context
- **OAuth removal scope**: Delete lines 277-331 of `backend/src/server.ts` including `MCP_OAUTH_BASE`, all 6 handlers (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, `/oauth/register`, `/register`, `/oauth/authorize`, `/oauth/token`), and the misleading comment block. Replace with a single `app.all()` loop returning 501 + structured JSON.
- **Bearer auth coexistence (CLI-045)**: Verify `mcpHandlers` validates Bearer tokens against `~/.rorca/mcp-token` — the fake OAuth token (`'rorca-local-access-token'`) must no longer be honored anywhere. Grep for that string and remove all references.
- **Invalid bearer != local admin fallback**: Per memory, if a bearer token is present but rejected, return `401 AUTH_ERROR` — do NOT silently inject `LOCAL_ADMIN`. Apply this rule to MCP route auth too.
- **Honest 501 response shape**: Use exact JSON `{ error, message, documentation }` from spec. Include `rorca mcp setup-claude` reference so clients get actionable feedback, not just a status code.
- **`rorca mcp diagnose-clients` command**: Add to `bin/rorca.ts` CLI dispatcher. Scan known paths: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS), `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (Linux), `%APPDATA%/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows), plus VS Code `settings.json` for `mcp.servers`. Parse JSON safely (try/catch per file), report which entries point at `/mcp` without Bearer headers.
- **API server staleness gotcha**: Per memory, tsx server does NOT hot-reload — after editing `server.ts`, manually `lsof -ti:3030 | xargs kill -9 && cd backend && npm run dev` before curl-testing the 501 responses. Stale server will keep serving old OAuth handlers and produce false positives.
- **Documentation updates**: README Security section + CLAUDE.md Security section must explain (a) Bearer-only model, (b) why OAuth was removed (honesty + CLI-045 conflict), (c) Claude Desktop limitation with Claude Code CLI as workaround. Use `claude mcp add ... --header 'Authorization: Bearer ...'` as canonical example.
- **Test coverage**: Add Jest test asserting all 6 OAuth paths return 501 with the documented JSON shape. Add regression test that valid Bearer token requests to `/mcp` still succeed end-to-end (CLI-045 unaffected).

userStories.title: AEGIS P1: MCP Audit Log + Per-Token Rate Limiting
userStories.description:
Even with CLI-045 through CLI-050 hardening, post-incident forensics requires visibility into MCP tool usage. And automated abuse (e.g. attacker who somehow obtained a token spamming `pipeline_trigger` to drain budgets) needs rate limiting.

**Step 1 — Add `mcp_audit_log` table** via timestamped migration `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>_mcp_audit_log.sql`:
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mcp_audit_log (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  ts TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  tool_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_tier TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (token_tier IN ('public', 'admin')),
  remote_addr TEXT,
  session_id TEXT,
  params_hash TEXT,  -- sha256 of normalized params (for grouping similar calls without leaking sensitive args)
  success BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  error_code TEXT,
  duration_ms INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX idx_mcp_audit_ts ON mcp_audit_log (ts DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_mcp_audit_token_tier ON mcp_audit_log (token_tier, ts DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_mcp_audit_tool ON mcp_audit_log (tool_name, ts DESC);
```

**Step 2 — Audit middleware** in `backend/src/lib/mcp-audit.ts`:
- `recordMcpCall(entry: McpAuditEntry): Promise<void>` — fire-and-forget insert, never blocks the response
- `paramsHash(params)` — `sha256(JSON.stringify(canonicalKeys(params)))` — keys sorted, values redacted for known-sensitive fields (password, token, key, secret, apiKey)

Wire into `mcp-http.ts` handler:
```typescript
const startMs = Date.now();
const result = await executeApiCall(...);
recordMcpCall({
  toolName,
  tokenTier: context.tier,
  remoteAddr: req.ip,
  sessionId: req.headers['mcp-session-id'],
  paramsHash: paramsHash(params),
  success: result.status < 400,
  errorCode: result.status >= 400 ? extractErrorCode(result.body) : null,
  durationMs: Date.now() - startMs,
}).catch(err => logger.warn({ err }, '[MCP Audit] Failed to record call'));
return result;
```

**Step 3 — Rate limiter** per token, per tool. Sliding window:
- Public token: 100 calls/min default (configurable via `RORCA_MCP_PUBLIC_RATE_LIMIT`)
- Admin token: 300 calls/min default (configurable via `RORCA_MCP_ADMIN_RATE_LIMIT`)
- Tool-specific overrides for expensive ops:
  - `rorca_pipeline_trigger`: 10/min (prevents budget drain)
  - `rorca_specs_generate`: 5/min (LLM cost)
  - `rorca_search`: 60/min

In-memory store (Map<tokenTier:tool, timestamps[]>), bounded by trim. On overflow → 429 with `Retry-After` header.

**Step 4 — Audit query API** (admin tier only):
- `GET /api/admin/mcp-audit` — paginated query with filters (tool, tier, success, since, until). Annotated `x-mcp-tier: admin` so the audit log itself is queryable via MCP (with admin token).
- `GET /api/admin/mcp-audit/summary` — counts grouped by tool + tier in a time window

**Step 5 — Anomaly detection (basic)**: at server startup + every 5 min, query for: (a) any tool called >1000 times in last hour, (b) any tool with error rate >50% in last hour, (c) any 401/403 storm (>50 in 5 min from same remote_addr). Log warnings; CLI-051 does not auto-block (avoid lockout). Auto-blocking is V2 work.

**Step 6 — Retention**: rows older than 90 days deleted by daily cron job. Configurable via `RORCA_MCP_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`.

**Step 7 — Privacy**: params_hash is sha256, not plaintext. Sensitive params (password, key, secret, token, apiKey) are NEVER stored. The audit log captures *that* a tool was called, not *what arguments*. For full param logging in development, opt-in via `RORCA_MCP_AUDIT_FULL_PARAMS=1` (off by default, never on in production).

## Context
- **Migration filename**: Use `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_mcp_audit_log.sql` (timestamp format) — sequential 001-079 already exist; new migrations MUST be timestamped to avoid parallel-branch collisions (see Notable Bug Fixes: "Duplicate migration 069 collision"). Place in `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/`.
- **WAL precedent for `ts` column**: Follow `wal_events` pattern — use `ts TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` (NOT `created_at`). Indexes on `(ts DESC)` match existing query patterns. API responses can alias `ts AS created_at` for consumers if needed.
- **Rate limiter pattern**: `backend/src/lib/rate-limiter.ts` already exists with sliding-window in-memory store keyed by `userId:method:path`. Extend or mirror that pattern for `tokenTier:tool` keys — do NOT introduce a new rate limit library. Skip enforcement when `NODE_ENV=test` unless `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true` (consistency with existing limiter).
- **MCP HTTP handler integration**: Wire audit + rate limit into `backend/src/lib/mcp-http.ts` (the HTTP transport), NOT the stdio server in `backend/src/mcp/server.ts`. Token tier comes from `mcp-auth.ts` context (public vs admin) — see existing `src/lib/mcp-auth.ts` (untracked file in working tree).
- **Fire-and-forget DB insert**: Use `.catch()` on the promise — never `await` the audit insert in the request path. DB outages must NOT break MCP calls. Log failures via existing pino logger pattern (`logger.warn({ err }, ...)`).
- **Sensitive param redaction**: `paramsHash()` must redact keys matching `/password|token|key|secret|apiKey/i` BEFORE `JSON.stringify` + sha256. Use sorted keys (`canonicalKeys`) for deterministic hashing — same params from different call sites produce same hash for grouping.
- **Admin route mount**: Add `/api/admin/mcp-audit` to existing admin router (check `backend/src/routes/admin.ts` or similar). Annotate with `@swagger` JSDoc + `x-mcp-tier: admin` extension so OpenAPI-to-MCP generator exposes it only under admin token (per API-First MCP architecture).
- **Retention cron**: Hook into existing `scheduler.ts` (cron runner for `pipeline_schedules`) — add a daily job, do NOT spawn a separate cron process. Use `RORCA_MCP_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` env var with default 90.
- **Anomaly detection**: Schedule via same `scheduler.ts` at 5-min interval. Emit warnings through existing logger; do NOT call `recordMcpCall` from anomaly checks (avoid recursive feedback). Explicitly NO auto-blocking in P1 to prevent lockout — document this in code comment.
- **Server staleness gotcha**: After adding new admin routes, manually kill+restart the API server (`lsof -ti:3030 | xargs kill -9 && cd backend && npm run dev`) — tsx does NOT hot-reload route additions, new routes return 404 until restart.
- **Type safety**: Define `McpAuditEntry` interface in `mcp-audit.ts` with strict types; no implicit any. Token tier must be typed `'public' | 'admin'` matching the CHECK constraint.
