userStories.title: AEGIS P1: Hardening Documentation + Threat Model in CLAUDE.md
userStories.description:
Capture the security architecture and threat model in CLAUDE.md so future contributors understand WHY the protections exist and don't undo them. Without this, the next refactor could re-introduce the auto-promotion footgun or remove the localhost guard 'because dev was painful'.

**Step 1 — Add Security section** to CLAUDE.md (top-level, after 'Architecture'):

```markdown
## Security Model (Project Aegis)

### Threat Model

Rorca runs on localhost as a single-user developer tool. The threats it must defend against:

1. **Drive-by browser attack** — User visits evil.com in a tab while Rorca is running. Page does `fetch('http://localhost:3030/mcp', ...)`. Defense: CORS origin allow-list (CLI-046), Bearer token (CLI-045).
2. **LAN attacker** — User on shared WiFi, attacker with route to :3030. Defense: 127.0.0.1 bind enforcement (CLI-046).
3. **Compromised MCP client** — User adds a malicious MCP integration. Defense: scoped public/admin tokens (CLI-049), audit log (CLI-051).
4. **Token leak** — User accidentally pastes token into Discord. Defense: scoped tiers limit blast radius (CLI-049), rotate-token command (CLI-045).
5. **Privilege escalation via auto-exposed routes** — Future @swagger annotation accidentally exposes admin route. Defense: opt-IN annotation gate (CLI-047), CI lint check.
6. **Insider abuse** — Authenticated client floods pipeline_trigger to drain budget. Defense: per-token rate limits (CLI-051).

### Defense Layers

1. **Origin lockdown** (CLI-046) — Browser-origin attacks blocked at CORS layer
2. **Localhost binding** (CLI-046) — Network attacks blocked at TCP layer
3. **Bearer token authentication** (CLI-045) — Unauthenticated clients blocked at HTTP layer
4. **Opt-IN tool annotations** (CLI-047) — Routes default-denied; explicit x-mcp-tier required for exposure
5. **Curated allow-list** (CLI-048) — Only ~40 of 414 routes are MCP-exposed; destructive ops permanently denied
6. **Scoped tier authorization** (CLI-049) — Public token cannot trigger admin operations
7. **Audit log + rate limit** (CLI-051) — Observable + bounded

### Default Stance

- Auth: `LOCAL_ADMIN` injected for browser/web UI calls (single-user tool)
- MCP: Bearer token REQUIRED (no fallback to LOCAL_ADMIN)
- Production deployments: set `AUTH_REQUIRED=true` to force JWT for all routes

### Adding a New MCP Tool (route author guide)

1. Add @swagger JSDoc as usual
2. Add `x-mcp-tier: public | admin` and `x-mcp-rationale: <why safe>`
3. Run `npm run lint:mcp` — must pass
4. PR review will scrutinize the rationale; expect pushback for anything touching: filesystem writes, env vars, credentials, code execution, network requests

### What's Permanently Denied (and Why)

- `/api/terminal/*` — PTY spawn = arbitrary code execution
- `/api/vault/*` — credential operations
- `/api/billing/*` — Stripe operations
- `/api/admin/*` — backups, license generation, embed-all
- `/api/skills/install*` — prompt injection vector (skills auto-injected into agent prompts)
- `/api/workspaces/{id}/env-vars` (mutations) — env injection vector
- `/api/webhooks/*` — signature spoofing/replay
- All DELETE except scoped story/comment deletes

### Token Management

- Public token: `~/.rorca/mcp-token` (mode 0600)
- Admin token: `~/.rorca/mcp-admin-token` (mode 0600)
- Generated at first run, never logged
- Rotation: `rorca mcp rotate-token --public | --admin | --all`
- Setup MCP client: `rorca mcp setup-claude [--admin]`
```

**Step 2 — Add `backend/src/lib/AGENTS.md`** governance entry: 'Files in `backend/src/lib/mcp-*.ts` are security-critical. Changes require: (a) explicit security review tag in PR, (b) updated threat model in CLAUDE.md, (c) regression tests in `__tests__/mcp-aegis.test.ts`.'

**Step 3 — Pull request template**. Add `.github/pull_request_template.md` (or update existing):
```markdown
## Security Checklist
- [ ] Does this PR add a new @swagger annotation? If so, did you add x-mcp-tier?
- [ ] Does this PR modify backend/src/lib/mcp-*.ts? If so, link the threat model section affected.
- [ ] Does this PR remove or weaken any of the 7 defense layers? If so, justify in detail.
```

**Step 4 — `rorca-mcp-incident-response.md`** runbook in `docs/security/`:
- How to detect token compromise (audit log queries)
- Rotation procedure (commands, expected disruption window)
- Forensics queries (recent admin tool calls, anomaly patterns)
- Disclosure template if user-facing

**Step 5 — Verify documentation accuracy**. Run `npm run lint:mcp` and confirm counts match what CLAUDE.md says. Run an end-to-end smoke test (curl from disallowed origin → 403, curl with public token + admin tool → 403, etc.) and capture in spec notes.

## Context
- **Insertion point**: Add the new "Security Model (Project Aegis)" section in CLAUDE.md immediately after the top-level "## Architecture" section and before "## Execution Engine — Core Identity" — preserve existing heading hierarchy and don't reflow unrelated content.
- **Cross-reference existing gotchas**: The current CLAUDE.md "Auth Middleware — Intentionally Bypassed" gotcha (in Critical Gotchas) is the canonical statement that `authRequired` is commented out; the new Security section's "Default Stance" must link/reference it rather than contradict it. Memory rule: invalid bearer tokens MUST return `401 AUTH_ERROR` and NEVER fall through to LOCAL_ADMIN — call this out explicitly in the Default Stance bullet.
- **Counts must be live, not hardcoded**: Acceptance criteria says ~25 public / ~15 admin, but step 5 requires `npm run lint:mcp` output to match. Run the lint command FIRST, capture exact counts, then write CLAUDE.md with those exact numbers. Re-run after writing to confirm. Do not ship "~25" if lint emits a precise count.
- **AGENTS.md location**: Per CLAUDE.md "Workspace Context Files — Root Level Required" gotcha, governance AGENTS.md files at the workspace root satisfy health checks; subdirectory AGENTS.md (e.g., `backend/src/lib/AGENTS.md`) does NOT count toward that check but IS valid as scoped governance for CIE/persona injection. Document this distinction in the new entry so future readers don't think it satisfies the root-level requirement.
- **PR template idempotency**: Check for existing `.github/pull_request_template.md` (or `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`) before creating — if one exists, append the Security Checklist section rather than overwriting.
- **Runbook directory**: `docs/security/` likely doesn't exist yet — create the directory. Use kebab-case filename per coding_style (`rorca-mcp-incident-response.md` already matches). Forensics queries should reference the audit log table created in CLI-051 (verify table name from that story's output before writing SQL examples).
- **Smoke test capture**: "Spec notes" means appending results to the spec JSON's `notes` field or a sibling `.md` log — confirm by reading the spec file at `forge/specs/approved/<spec-id>.json` first. Capture exact curl commands + response codes (403 for disallowed origin, 403 for public-token-on-admin-tool, 401 for missing token, 200 for valid) so future audits can replay them.
- **Documentation-only constraint**: AC explicitly says "No new MCP tools introduced by this story." Do NOT add `@swagger` annotations, do NOT modify route files, do NOT touch `backend/src/lib/mcp-*.ts` logic. Only edit: `CLAUDE.md`, `backend/src/lib/AGENTS.md`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `docs/security/rorca-mcp-incident-response.md`.
- **Conventional commit**: Use `docs:` prefix (per output_preferences) — e.g., `docs: add Project Aegis threat model and incident response runbook`. Keep PR under 400 lines (likely fine for docs-only).

userStories.title: OPEN-CORE P0: Public API Contract Enforcement — break-detection CI gate
userStories.description:
**COMMERCIAL CRITICAL.** Once routes are annotated `x-rorca-public-api: true` (CLI-048), they become the **stable open-source CLI contract**. External consumers (forks, integrations, the open-source CLI itself) call these routes and depend on their behavior. Breaking changes to public-api routes break the entire open-source ecosystem — and worse, give legal grounds for downstream consumers to claim breach of API stability if marketed as such.

This story adds CI-time **contract enforcement**: a snapshot of public-api routes is committed to the repo (`docs/OPEN_API_CONTRACT.md` + `docs/openapi-public-snapshot.json`), and any PR that changes a public-api route fails CI unless explicitly acknowledged via a versioned breaking-change marker.

**Step 1 — Generate canonical contract artifact** at build time:
```bash
npm run build:contract
# → reads /api/docs/openapi.json from a running server
# → filters for x-rorca-public-api: true routes
# → writes docs/openapi-public-snapshot.json (canonical, sorted by path)
# → writes docs/OPEN_API_CONTRACT.md (human-readable)
```
Implemented in `scripts/build-public-contract.ts`. Both files are committed to the repo.

**Step 2 — Contract structure**. `docs/openapi-public-snapshot.json` shape:
```json
{
  "contractVersion": "1.0.0",
  "generatedAt": "2026-05-01T...",
  "routes": [
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/api/specs",
      "parameters": [...],
      "responseSchema": { ... },
      "hash": "sha256:..."
    }
  ]
}
```
The `hash` is sha256 of the canonical JSON of method+path+parameters+responseSchema. ANY change to those fields changes the hash → CI detects breaking change.

**Step 3 — CI break-detection** in `scripts/check-contract-stability.ts`:
1. Read committed `docs/openapi-public-snapshot.json` (the baseline)
2. Generate fresh snapshot from current code
3. Compare:
   - Removed public route → BREAKING (fail CI)
   - Changed hash on existing route → BREAKING (fail CI)
   - Added public route → ALLOWED (additive non-breaking)
   - Removed public-api flag from a route (downgraded to auth/paid/denied) → BREAKING (fail CI)
4. Print human-readable diff showing what changed

**Step 4 — Breaking-change override**. Sometimes you genuinely need to break the contract (security fix, deprecated cleanup). The override is explicit:
- File `docs/contract-breaking-changes.md` lists each breaking change with: date, route, justification, migration path
- Each entry has a marker: `<!-- contract-break: 2026-06-15 GET /api/specs/{id} -->`
- CI script reads markers; if a breaking change is matched by a marker dated within 30 days of the PR, allow it
- Markers older than 30 days from the PR date REJECT (forces fresh justification per change)
- Major version bump in `package.json` required when contract-breaking-changes.md gets new entries

**Step 5 — Contract version bumping**:
- Adding public route → minor bump (1.0 → 1.1)
- Breaking change → major bump (1.x → 2.0), requires migration guide entry
- Captured in `contractVersion` field of the snapshot

**Step 6 — Wire into CI** at `.github/workflows/contract-check.yml`:
```yaml
name: Public API Contract
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm run dev:server &
      - run: sleep 5  # wait for server
      - run: npm run check:contract
```

**Step 7 — Document in CONTRIBUTING.md** (create if missing): "The Rorca Public API Contract is the stable interface for the open-source CLI. Breaking changes require: (1) entry in docs/contract-breaking-changes.md, (2) major version bump, (3) migration guide. See CLI-054."

**Step 8 — Bootstrap**. Initial commit of CLI-054 generates the first snapshot — this becomes the v1.0 baseline. All subsequent PRs are diffed against this.

## Context
- **Snapshot generation must hit a live server**: `/api/docs/openapi.json` is served by Express at runtime via `swagger.ts` (auto-generated from `@swagger` JSDoc). Script must spawn or assume a running backend on :3030 — there is no static OpenAPI file to read. Wait for `/api/health` 200 before fetching, not a fixed `sleep 5`.
- **Canonical JSON hashing is fragile**: Use a stable stringifier (e.g. `json-stable-stringify`) — `JSON.stringify` does not guarantee key order across Node versions, and parameters arrays from swagger-jsdoc may come in route-declaration order. Sort `parameters` by `name`, sort object keys recursively, then sha256. Otherwise hashes drift on every run and CI is permanently red.
- **Filter must match CLI-048's flag exactly**: `x-rorca-public-api: true` is a vendor extension on the operation object (not the path object). Verify against CLI-048's annotation site before filtering — wrong nesting = empty snapshot = silent contract collapse.
- **30-day marker window is PR-date relative, not commit-date**: Compute via `process.env.GITHUB_PR_CREATED_AT` or `gh pr view` in the workflow; do not use `new Date()` at script runtime (breaks reruns of old PRs). Marker format `<!-- contract-break: YYYY-MM-DD METHOD /path -->` must be parsed strictly — regex anchor on line start, validate ISO date.
- **Major version bump enforcement**: Read `package.json` version on PR HEAD vs base branch; if `contract-breaking-changes.md` has new entries (line-diff), require base→head major increment. Use semver parse, not string compare.
- **Additive-only is not always safe**: A new public route added then later removed is still a break. Snapshot-by-hash naturally handles this, but document that "added public route" only passes CI on the introducing PR — subsequent removal triggers BREAKING as expected.
- **Conventional commits + PR size**: Use `feat(contract):` and `chore(contract):` prefixes; this story will likely exceed 400 lines (two scripts + workflow + docs + bootstrap snapshot) — split bootstrap snapshot commit from script commit if reviewer asks, but keep in one PR for atomicity.
- **No auth interference**: Auth middleware is globally disabled (per CLAUDE.md), so the CI server fetch of `/api/docs/openapi.json` works without tokens. Do NOT add auth handling to the build script — it will break when auth is re-enabled in cloud mode but that's a separate concern (CLI-048 territory).
- **TypeScript strict + absolute imports**: Both scripts go in `scripts/` (already a convention in repo); use `tsx` to run, not `ts-node`. Type the snapshot shape explicitly — do not `any`-cast OpenAPI response.
- **Worker not required**: This is pure HTTP introspection of the API — no pg-boss jobs, no execution-engine spawning. Do not start the worker in CI; just `npm run dev:server` (or equivalent server-only script — confirm it exists, may need to add a `dev:server-only` npm script that skips the worker).

userStories.title: OPEN-CORE P0: License Header Enforcement — MIT for CLI, BSL for backend
userStories.description:
**LEGAL CRITICAL.** Open-core mixes two licenses in one repo: `packages/rorca-cli/` (MIT/Apache 2.0 — open source) and `backend/` + `src/` (BSL 1.1 — proprietary). Without enforcement, a contributor could (a) copy proprietary code into the CLI package, (b) miss license headers on new files, (c) accidentally publish proprietary code to npm. This story automates license boundary enforcement.

**Step 1 — License files** at repo root:
- `LICENSE` — currently BSL-1.1 (covers root/backend/src). Verify content matches https://mariadb.com/bsl11/ template.
- `packages/rorca-cli/LICENSE` — NEW, **MIT License** (chosen over Apache 2.0 for simplicity; permissive enough for npm distribution)
- `LICENSE-NOTICES.md` at root — explains the dual-license: "This repository is dual-licensed. Files under packages/rorca-cli/ are MIT. All other files (backend/, src/, scripts/, etc.) are BSL-1.1. See individual LICENSE files in each tree."

**Step 2 — License headers on every source file** in their respective trees:

For `packages/rorca-cli/**/*.ts` (MIT):
```typescript
/**
 * Copyright (c) 2026 Rorca Inc.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
 */
```

For `backend/**/*.ts` and `src/**/*.ts` (BSL-1.1):
```typescript
/**
 * Copyright (c) 2026 Rorca Inc.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BUSL-1.1
 * Licensed under the Business Source License 1.1.
 * See LICENSE file in the project root for full license text.
 */
```

**Step 3 — Header enforcement script** at `scripts/check-license-headers.ts`:
1. Glob `packages/rorca-cli/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}` — verify each has `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`
2. Glob `backend/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}` and `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}` — verify each has `SPDX-License-Identifier: BUSL-1.1`
3. Reject if any file has the WRONG header (proprietary code in CLI package, or vice versa)
4. Allow files in `__tests__/` to inherit parent dir's license
5. Skip `node_modules/`, `dist/`, generated files

**Step 4 — Cross-license import check** at `scripts/check-license-boundaries.ts`:
1. Parse all imports in `packages/rorca-cli/**/*.ts`
2. For each import, resolve the target file
3. If target is in `backend/` or `src/` → REJECT (CLI cannot import proprietary code)
4. Allowed: imports from npm packages, from `packages/rorca-cli/` itself, from `packages/rorca-core/` (if created later as MIT shared)
5. Specifically reject: `import x from '../../backend/...'`, `import y from '../../src/...'`

**Step 5 — npm pack verification**. CLI-037 already verifies pack contents. Extend to also verify:
- The published tarball does NOT include any BSL-licensed file
- All files in the tarball have `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` headers (when shipping `@rorca/cli` standalone)
- Note: For Phase A (single rorca package), CLI code lives in `packages/rorca-cli/` but ships AS-IS in the rorca npm package which is BSL-licensed at the root. The MIT-licensed CLI files retain their MIT headers but the overall npm package is governed by the root LICENSE (BSL-1.1) for the bundled artifacts. This is accurate and legal — MIT files in a BSL package are fine; what's NOT fine is BSL files in an MIT-only package.

**Step 6 — When CLI is extracted to standalone `@rorca/cli` (post-V1)**: the standalone package's tarball contains ONLY MIT files. CLI-055 enforcement applies to that future state too — running `npm pack` from `packages/rorca-cli/` should produce a 100%-MIT tarball.

**Step 7 — Wire CI** at `.github/workflows/license-check.yml`:
```yaml
- run: npm run check:licenses     # CLI-055 step 3
- run: npm run check:license-boundaries  # CLI-055 step 4
```

**Step 8 — Documentation in `LICENSE-NOTICES.md`**:
- Why open-core (the LangChain/PostHog 2026 playbook)
- Which directories are which license
- How to contribute to MIT vs BSL portions (CLAs, contributor agreements)
- Build artifacts and which license they fall under

**Step 9 — Migration risk note**: existing files under `backend/` and `src/` may not have BSL headers today. CLI-055 implementation must add headers to all existing files before turning on enforcement, OR enforcement starts with a snapshot (only newly-changed files require headers). Recommend: add headers to all files in a single bulk PR before turning on CI enforcement, to avoid 1000+ files marked as 'missing header' on day 1.

## Context
- **Repo structure**: No `packages/rorca-cli/` exists yet — CLI-055 depends on the open-core split being completed first; verify prerequisite stories (likely CLI-001/CLI-037) have created the package boundary before adding license enforcement.
- **Bulk header migration risk**: 32 route files + 70+ migrations + 22 panels + dozens of `lib/` modules need BSL headers in one PR. Use a codemod script (ts-morph or simple regex prepend) — do NOT hand-edit. Skip already-headered files (idempotent).
- **Glob exclusions**: Header check must skip `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.rorca/`, `forge/specs/`, `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/*.sql` (SQL files use `--` comments, not `/** */`), generated OpenAPI artifacts, and `*.test.ts` snapshots. Use the same ignore list as ESLint.
- **Boundary check resolver**: Use TypeScript compiler API or `resolve` package to resolve relative imports — regex-only parsing misses re-exports, dynamic imports, and `import type`. Treat `import type` from BSL as still forbidden (type leakage = API surface leakage).
- **Migration file caveat**: SQL migrations in `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/` are BSL but cannot host JSDoc headers. Either exclude them from the check or accept a SQL-comment header variant (`-- SPDX-License-Identifier: BUSL-1.1`).
- **Conventional commits**: Use `chore: add license headers` for bulk migration PR, `feat: enforce license boundaries in CI` for the script + workflow PR. Keep them separate to keep PR size under 400 lines (engineering principle) — though the bulk header PR will exceed this; flag in PR description as one-time mechanical change.
- **CI workflow placement**: `.github/workflows/license-check.yml` is a NEW workflow. Verify it runs on `pull_request` AND `push: main`, and that it's required in branch protection rules (otherwise enforcement is advisory only).
- **Tarball verification**: Extend existing CLI-037 `npm pack` test rather than duplicating logic. Use `npm pack --dry-run --json` to enumerate tarball contents without writing to disk.
- **Gotcha — tsx/Vite banner injection**: If any build step uses esbuild/Vite `banner` option, it may strip or duplicate license headers on bundled output. Check `vite.config.ts` and any esbuild configs; preserve headers via `legalComments: 'inline'` or `banner` config.

userStories.title: [DEPRECATED — replaced by CLI-033] rorca db: Docker sidecar lifecycle management for Postgres+AGE
userStories.description:
Create `backend/src/lib/db-sidecar.ts` and wire `rorca db` CLI commands to manage the Rorca Postgres+AGE Docker container. This container is the storage layer for the full Command Center stack: relational data (pg), graph memory (Apache AGE), queue (pg-boss), vector search (pgvector).

**Container spec**: Docker image `apache/age:latest` (falls back to `postgres:16-alpine` if AGE image unavailable — AGE extension can be loaded separately). Container name: `rorca-db`. Port mapping: `5432:5432`. Volume: `rorca-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data` (named volume, persists across container restarts). Environment: `POSTGRES_DB=rorca POSTGRES_USER=rorca POSTGRES_PASSWORD=rorca`. This matches the default `DATABASE_URL=postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5432/rorca` in `.env.example`.

**Exported async functions in `db-sidecar.ts`**:
- `dbStart(): Promise<void>` — checks Docker is running (`docker info` 3s timeout), inspects `rorca-db` container. If exists+stopped: `docker start rorca-db`. If not exists: `docker run -d --name rorca-db -p 5432:5432 -v rorca-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data -e POSTGRES_DB=rorca -e POSTGRES_USER=rorca -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=rorca apache/age:latest`. Polls `docker exec rorca-db pg_isready -U rorca` every 1s up to 15s. Prints `✓ Database ready at localhost:5432`.
- `dbStop(): Promise<void>` — `docker stop rorca-db`. Prints `✓ Database stopped`.
- `dbStatus(): Promise<{ running: boolean; containerExists: boolean; version: string | null }>` — `docker inspect rorca-db --format '{{.State.Status}}'`. Never throws.
- `dbReset(): Promise<void>` — prints `⚠ This will destroy ALL Rorca data. Continue? [y/N]`, requires 'y'. Stops+removes container, removes volume, calls `dbStart()`.
- `dbLogs(tail: number = 50): Promise<void>` — `docker logs --tail <n> --follow rorca-db` with stdio:inherit.

**Docker not available path**: if `docker info` fails, print: `✗ Docker not found.\n\nRorca requires Docker for its database (Apache AGE graph extension).\n\nInstall options:\n  macOS:  https://orbstack.dev (recommended — lighter than Docker Desktop)\n  macOS:  https://docs.docker.com/desktop/mac/\n  Linux:  https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/\n\nAlternatively, bring your own Postgres with AGE installed:\n  Set DATABASE_URL in backend/.env and run: rorca start --no-db`

**Graceful degradation when AGE not available**: If Postgres is running but `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS age` fails (e.g. bring-your-own postgres without AGE), the knowledge graph routes in `backend/src/routes/` catch the error and return `503 { error: 'AGE extension not available', code: 'AGE_NOT_INSTALLED' }` instead of crashing. All non-graph routes continue working normally. This is the 'Lite' path — full relational and queue features, no graph traversal.

## Context
- **DEPRECATED story**: This is marked replaced by CLI-033 in the title — confirm with user before implementing. Skipping is likely the correct action.
- **CLI entry point**: `bin/rorca.ts` is the existing CLI; add `db` subcommand dispatcher there. Keep command handlers thin — delegate all logic to `backend/src/lib/db-sidecar.ts`.
- **Spawn pattern**: Use `child_process.spawn` (not `exec`) for `docker` calls. Reference existing patterns in `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts` (subprocess spawning, timeout via SIGTERM→SIGKILL, stdio handling). For `docker logs --follow`, use `stdio: 'inherit'` so Ctrl+C propagates.
- **Docker detection**: `docker info` with 3s timeout via `AbortController` or `child_process` timeout option — never let CLI hang if Docker daemon is down.
- **Confirmation prompt** (`dbReset`): Use `readline` from Node stdlib for `[y/N]` — do NOT add `inquirer`/`prompts` deps. Default to "no" on empty input.
- **AGE graceful degradation**: Knowledge graph routes live in `backend/src/routes/` (look for files calling `setupAgeSession()`). Wrap `CREATE EXTENSION age` and Cypher calls in try/catch, return `503 { error, code: 'AGE_NOT_INSTALLED' }`. Critical: on AGE failure path, still RESET `search_path = rorca, public` per the AGE pool poison gotcha (see MEMORY.md).
- **Port conflict**: Existing dev setup uses native Postgres on 5432 (per memory: user prefers native over Docker). Container will fail to bind if native pg is running — surface this clearly: "Port 5432 in use. Stop native Postgres or use --no-db with custom DATABASE_URL."
- **Errors**: Use `AppError` subclasses from `backend/src/lib/errors.ts` for any thrown errors (`ValidationError`, `ConflictError`). Never expose raw Docker stderr to user — wrap with friendly message + hint.
- **Testing**: Backend uses Jest. Mock `child_process.spawn` for unit tests; add integration test guarded by `process.env.DOCKER_AVAILABLE` env check so CI without Docker doesn't fail.
- **No tsx watch for long-running**: If `rorca start` boots Express after `dbStart()`, use plain `tsx` not `tsx watch` per `feedback_tsx_watch.md`.

userStories.description:
Extend the `rorca init` command (in bin/rorca.ts, CLI-025) so it doubles as the zero-to-running first-time setup wizard. Goal: a developer runs `npm install -g @rorca/cli && rorca init` and is ready to forge specs in under 5 minutes.

**Sequence** (each step prints a status line):
1. **Check Docker** — call `dbStatus()`. If Docker not running: print install instructions (OrbStack + Docker Desktop links) and exit 1.
2. **Pull image** (only if container doesn't exist) — run `docker pull apache/age:latest` with pipe to stdout so progress is visible. Print `Pulling Rorca database image (~200MB, first run only)...` before pull.
3. **Start database** — call `dbStart()`. Waits for pg_isready. Prints `✓ Database ready at localhost:5432`.
4. **Enable AGE extension** — run `docker exec rorca-db psql -U rorca -d rorca -c 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS age; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;'`. Print `✓ Graph + vector extensions enabled`.
5. **Scaffold workspace** — create `.rorca/config.json` (empty object `{}`), `AGENTS.md` (starter template: one-liner header + 'Add your file governance rules here'), `MEMORY.md` (empty ledger: `# Memory\n\n_No entries yet._`), `.rorca/skills/` directory. Skip files that already exist (idempotent).
6. **Print next steps** — exactly this block:
```
Rorca is ready! Next steps:
  1. rorca start          # Start backend + worker
  2. rorca doctor         # Verify all systems  
  3. rorca auth login     # Connect pi to a provider
  4. rorca forge <brief>  # Generate your first spec
```

**Flags**:
- `--skip-docker` — skip steps 1-4. Prints: `Skipping Docker setup — ensure AGE + pgvector are enabled: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS age; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;`
- `--path <dir>` — target directory for workspace scaffold (defaults to cwd)

**Idempotency**: `rorca init` is safe to run multiple times. Container already running → skips pull/start. Files already exist → skips creation (prints 'Already exists: AGENTS.md'). The AGE/vector CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS is always idempotent.

## Context
- **Story is DEPRECATED** — title indicates this work is folded into CLI-033 + CLI-040 + CLI-044. Verify with spec owner before implementing; likely should be deleted rather than executed.
- **Edit `bin/rorca.ts`** (already modified per git status) — extend existing `rorca init` command from CLI-025; do not create a new command file. Use Commander.js patterns already established.

userStories.title: MCP ASYNC P0: spec_jobs table + JobStatus state machine for long-running operations
userStories.description:
Create a `spec_jobs` table to track async LLM operations (enrich, match-skills, suggest-skills, suggest-models, detect-dependencies, knowledge-graph, add-stories) so MCP clients can fire-and-poll instead of holding open a single HTTP connection for 5-15 minutes. The current synchronous model causes MCP client timeouts (Anthropic-side, ~60-120s) that abort runs even though the server-side LLM call would complete fine.

## Schema (PostgreSQL migration, timestamp prefix YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_create_spec_jobs.sql)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS spec_jobs (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  spec_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (job_type IN ('enrich','match-skills','suggest-skills','suggest-models','detect-dependencies','knowledge-graph','add-stories','validate','score')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','running','completed','failed','cancelled')),
  progress_current INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  progress_total INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  progress_message TEXT,
  request_payload JSONB,
  result_payload JSONB,
  error_message TEXT,
  started_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  finished_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_spec_jobs_workspace_spec ON spec_jobs(workspace_id, spec_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_spec_jobs_status ON spec_jobs(status) WHERE status IN ('pending','running');
```

## State machine
- `pending` → `running` (when worker picks up)
- `running` → `completed` (success) | `failed` (LLM error) | `cancelled` (user cancel)
- Terminal states: `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`
- `progress_current/total/message` updated mid-run (e.g., "Enriching story 23/53...") for UI streaming

## DB module (`backend/src/db/spec-jobs.ts`)
- `createJob(workspaceId, specId, jobType, requestPayload): Promise<SpecJob>` — INSERT, return row with UUID
- `getJob(jobId): Promise<SpecJob | null>` — SELECT by UUID
- `updateJobStatus(jobId, status, fields?): Promise<void>` — UPDATE status + optional progress/result/error
- `listActiveJobs(workspaceId, specId?): Promise<SpecJob[]>` — for UI polling list
- `cleanupStaleJobs(): Promise<number>` — mark `running` jobs older than 30min as `failed` (worker crash recovery, like `recoverStaleJobs` pattern)

## Why this story is the foundation
Without `spec_jobs`, you can't make enrich/match-skills async — the LLM result has nowhere to land. Subsequent stories (CLI-058 worker, CLI-059 endpoints, CLI-060 MCP tools) all depend on this table existing. Stale-job cleanup pattern follows `pg-boss` worker conventions already used in `worker.ts`.

## Out of scope
- The actual job execution (CLI-058)
- New HTTP endpoints (CLI-059)
- MCP tool changes (CLI-060)
- Job cancellation API (folded into CLI-059)

userStories.title: MCP ASYNC P0: pg-boss worker handlers for spec:enrich, spec:match-skills, spec:suggest-skills
userStories.description:
Add pg-boss queue handlers for the 3 most-impacted long-running spec operations so they can run async. The existing synchronous LLM call (currently inside `POST /api/specs/:specId/enrich` etc.) gets extracted into a worker function that the queue handler invokes.

## Queue names
- `spec:enrich`
- `spec:match-skills`
- `spec:suggest-skills`

(Other slow operations — suggest-models, detect-dependencies, knowledge-graph, add-stories — get queues in CLI-059 follow-up if needed; start with the 3 that timeout most often per memory: enrich is the worst at 7min for 53-story spec.)

## Worker file (`backend/src/lib/spec-job-worker.ts`)
- `registerSpecJobHandlers(boss: PgBoss)` — one handler per queue, called from `worker.ts` at startup
- Each handler:
  1. Receive job payload `{ jobId, specId, workspaceId }`
  2. `updateJobStatus(jobId, 'running', { startedAt: new Date() })`
  3. Wrap the existing route logic in try/catch
  4. On progress checkpoints (e.g., per-story enrich), call `updateJobStatus(jobId, 'running', { progress: { current, total, message } })`
  5. On success: `updateJobStatus(jobId, 'completed', { resultPayload, finishedAt })`
  6. On error: `updateJobStatus(jobId, 'failed', { errorMessage, finishedAt })`

## Refactoring existing route logic
Extract LLM call + spec-write logic from `backend/src/routes/specs.ts` into pure functions in a new `backend/src/lib/spec-job-handlers.ts`:
- `runEnrichJob(workspaceId, specId, onProgress?): Promise<EnrichResult>`
- `runMatchSkillsJob(workspaceId, specId, onProgress?): Promise<MatchSkillsResult>`
- `runSuggestSkillsJob(workspaceId, specId, onProgress?): Promise<SuggestSkillsResult>`

These are reusable by both the sync routes (kept for backward compat in CLI-059) and the worker.

## Worker integration
In `backend/src/worker.ts`, after existing pg-boss setup, call `registerSpecJobHandlers(boss)`. Worker process now handles BOTH pipeline runs and spec jobs.

## Why pg-boss (not setImmediate or new worker process)
- Already running, already handles graceful shutdown
- Survives backend restarts (jobs persist in DB)
- Cancellation via existing `pgboss.cancel(jobId)` pattern
- Heartbeat + dead-job recovery battle-tested
- Avoids the OpenAI-style "worker stale after merge" memory bug since we use the same worker process

## Out of scope
- New HTTP endpoints (CLI-059)
- MCP tool changes to call async (CLI-060)
- UI progress streaming via SSE (folded into CLI-059)

userStories.title: MCP ASYNC P0: async HTTP endpoints — POST .../enrich/async + GET /spec-jobs/:id + SSE stream
userStories.description:
Expose the worker behind 3 new endpoints so MCP clients (and the UI) can fire-and-poll. Keep the existing sync endpoints for backward compatibility (with the timeout removed in the parent fix), but make async the recommended path.

## New endpoints

### POST /api/specs/:specId/enrich/async
Request: `{ workspaceId }`
Response 202: `{ jobId, status: 'pending', pollUrl: '/api/spec-jobs/<uuid>', streamUrl: '/api/spec-jobs/<uuid>/stream' }`
Behavior: createJob → boss.send('spec:enrich', { jobId, specId, workspaceId }) → return immediately

Same pattern for:
- POST /api/specs/:specId/match-skills/async
- POST /api/specs/:specId/suggest-skills/async

### GET /api/spec-jobs/:jobId
Response 200: `{ id, specId, workspaceId, jobType, status, progress: { current, total, message }, result, error, startedAt, finishedAt, createdAt }`
Behavior: SELECT from spec_jobs. Returns 404 if not found, 200 always otherwise (status field carries terminal state).

### GET /api/spec-jobs/:jobId/stream (SSE)
Response: text/event-stream
Behavior:
- On connect, send current state immediately (event: snapshot)
- Subscribe to a named pub/sub channel (use existing `sse-hub.ts` pattern with `spec_job:<jobId>` topic)
- Worker fires `broadcastAll({ type: 'spec_job_progress', jobId, ... })` on each onProgress + state change
- On terminal status, send final event then close connection

### POST /api/spec-jobs/:jobId/cancel
Request: empty
Response 200: `{ ok: true }` or 409 if job already terminal
Behavior: pgboss.cancel(<bossJobId stored in spec_jobs.boss_job_id>) + updateJobStatus(jobId, 'cancelled')

## Worker integration (CLI-058 enhancement)
When the worker creates a spec_jobs row in CLI-058, also pass the pg-boss job ID through and store as spec_jobs.boss_job_id (add column in CLI-057 migration). This lets cancel propagate.

## OpenAPI annotations
Add full @swagger blocks for all 4 new endpoints so MCP auto-generation picks them up as new tools (rorca_specs_by_id_enrich_async, rorca_spec_jobs_by_id, rorca_spec_jobs_by_id_stream, rorca_spec_jobs_by_id_cancel).

## Out of scope
- MCP tool wrapper logic (CLI-060)
- UI changes to use async path (separate UX spec)

userStories.title: MCP ASYNC P0: switch MCP tools (rorca_enrich_spec, rorca_match_skills) to fire-and-poll
userStories.description:
Update the rorca MCP server to use the async endpoints by default so MCP clients no longer hit Anthropic's connection timeout. The MCP tool now: (1) POST .../enrich/async to get jobId, (2) poll GET /spec-jobs/:id every 2s, (3) return final result when status is terminal. The polling loop runs server-side in the rorca MCP process — the connection between MCP client and rorca MCP stays alive via heartbeats but the actual LLM call is decoupled.

## Tools updated
- `rorca_enrich_spec` (handwritten in backend/src/mcp/server.ts ~line 3192)
- `rorca_match_skills` if exists, else add as new tool wrapping match-skills/async
- Auto-generated tools in backend/src/lib/mcp-http.ts: detect that path ends in /enrich, /match-skills, or /suggest-skills and switch to /async + poll loop

## Polling loop helper
`async function pollSpecJob(jobId: string, options?: { intervalMs?: number; maxWaitMs?: number; onProgress?: (state: SpecJob) => void }): Promise<SpecJob>`
- Defaults: intervalMs=2000, maxWaitMs=1_800_000 (30min absolute upper bound; rare for legitimate jobs)
- GET /api/spec-jobs/:jobId on each poll
- Return immediately when status in [completed, failed, cancelled]
- Throw on maxWaitMs exceeded (different from timeout — this is a server-side ceiling, not an Anthropic-side cutoff)

## MCP client UX
The MCP client sees one tool call that takes 7 minutes to return — but no timeout because the rorca MCP server keeps the connection alive via the polling loop and only returns when work is done. (MCP tool calls support long durations as long as the underlying transport stays connected; the previous problem was the Anthropic client closing the underlying HTTPS request, not the MCP protocol itself.)

Future story (out of scope): emit MCP progress notifications via the official protocol so clients can show "23/53 stories enriched" mid-flight.

## Out of scope
- MCP progress notifications (separate story when MCP SDK supports server→client progress events)
- UI changes (UI uses HTTP endpoints directly, not MCP)
- New MCP tools for cancellation (low priority — server-side cancel still works via DB)
